Technical integration guide

Graine in-app agents: integrating apps and websites

Everything your engineers need to put a Graine agent inside your mobile app and on your website, from the dashboard to the store submission: install, permissions, CallKit and Android call notifications, identity and memory, chat, voice, components, screen context and actions, WhatsApp-style calls in both directions, scheduled calls, several agents in one app, the complete SDK reference, testing and go-live.

Date 14 October 2026 For mobile and web engineers, QA and release managers Server needed none — a publishable key and the SDKs
PlatformPackageVersionWhere it comes from
iOS (Swift)GraineInApp — Swift package; CocoaPods pod GraineInApp0.7.0https://github.com/GraineAI/inapp-ios
Android (Kotlin, Java)ai.graine:inapp-android0.7.0Maven Central
Fluttergraine_inapp0.7.0pub.dev
Kotlin Multiplatformai.graine:inapp-kmp, ai.graine:inapp-kmp-compose0.7.0Maven Central

Every version above is read from the package files themselves: Version.swift and the podspec (iOS), GRAINE_VERSION (Android, Kotlin Multiplatform), pubspec.yaml (Flutter), package.json (React Native) and GraineAgent.version in the loader.

1.Start here — no meeting needed

This guide, the SDK references and the demo apps are written so that your team can integrate Graine in-app agents on its own, with no kick-off call. Follow this page in order: a first conversation with your agent in about 30 minutes, then WhatsApp-style calls in both directions, then go-live. Each step links to the part of the guide that explains it in full.

1.1What you receive

ItemWhat it is for
This integration guide (HTML and PDF)Every platform end to end: the dashboard set-up, install and permissions, identity and memory, chat and voice, calls both ways, scheduling, several agents, testing and go-live.
One SDK reference per platform — iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, Kotlin Multiplatform and the websiteEvery public function and type of that SDK: parameters, responses with example values, errors, events, and a short example for each function.
The demo apps (Graine-InApp-Demo-0.7.0.zip)A working app per platform. Each folder's README and RUN-THE-DEMO.md explain how to run it; an offline mode shows every screen with no workspace or key (the demo apps).
Your Graine workspaceYour team is invited by email. Your agents, their publishable keys (Agent → Embed & Widgets → Install), Call History and every setting this guide names are there.

  1. This page.
  2. How it works end to end — the parts, and what happens in a conversation and in a call.
  3. Dashboard setup — the agent, the key and Allowed domains, the Garage, memory, calls and scheduling.
  4. Install and set up — only your platform's part: requirements, install, permissions, initialisation.

  6. WhatsApp-style calls and scheduled calls — the two directions of a call.

  8. Testing end to end, then the go-live checklist.

1.3A first success in 30 minutes: the agent answers

  1. Open your agent in the dashboard → Embed & Widgets → Install. Copy the publishable key (pk_live_…) and, for a website, the agent ID (the Install tab).
  2. Allow where it runs in Allowed domains: app:// for a mobile app; localhost while you try a web page on your computer (remove it before go-live).
  3. Add the agent — pick one path below. For a native app, install the SDK first (your platform's install step).
  4. Run it and talk. Tap the agent (the launcher, or the bar) and speak, or type in the chat. The agent answers in your design. The conversation appears in the agent's Call History.
HTMLWebsite — before </body>
<script src="https://www.graine.ai/embed/v1.js"></script>
<script>
  GraineAgent.load({ agentId: "your-website-agent-id", publishableKey: "pk_live_…" });
</script>
React Native · TypeScriptReact Native — App.tsx
<GraineProvider baseUrl="https://www.graine.ai" publishableKey="pk_live_…">
  <AppNavigator />
  <GraineVoiceLauncher webView={WebView} active={open} autoStart>
    {(api) => (open ? <GraineVoiceBar api={api} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} /> : null)}
  </GraineVoiceLauncher>
  {!open && <GraineLauncherButton onPress={() => setOpen(true)} />}
</GraineProvider>
iOS · SwiftiOS — at launch, and on your root view
GraineInApp.configure(GraineConfig(baseUrl: "https://www.graine.ai", publishableKey: "pk_live_…"))
RootView().overlay(GraineAgentBar())
Android · KotlinAndroid — Application.onCreate, and your activity
GraineInApp.init(this, GraineConfig(baseUrl = "https://www.graine.ai", publishableKey = "pk_live_…"))
root.addView(GraineAgentBarView(this), FrameLayout.LayoutParams(MATCH_PARENT, WRAP_CONTENT, Gravity.BOTTOM))

Nothing answers? The SDK says why in its log (turn on debug in the configuration): the usual causes are a key copied wrongly, a missing app:// or host in Allowed domains, and a microphone permission not granted. Troubleshooting lists each with its fix.

1.4WhatsApp-style calls end to end: a checklist

Calls work in two directions: the customer calls the agent from a button in your app, and Graine rings the customer at a booked time, even with the phone locked. Work through the list on real phones; each step links to its instructions.

StepDone when
1. Create your push credentials — an APNs key (iOS) and a Firebase service account (Android), click by click in Create your credentials — and upload them in Workspace settings → In-app callingEach platform shows Verified
2. Wire the calls in your app: CallKit and PushKit on iOS, the push handler and the manifest on Android, the calls package on React Native and Flutter (hosted ringing); sign in as a test customer with identify()The app runs with the calls configured and a customer identified; step 6 proves the wiring
3. The customer calls the agent: add a call button with startCall (startCall)The call screen opens and the agent answers
4. Turn on booking in Agent → Calls & scheduling: who may book, the calling window, the call's name (Calls & scheduling)Saved; schedulingRules.usersCanBook is true in the app
5. Book a call — from the app with scheduleCall, by the agent in a conversation, or by your team with Schedule a call (scheduled calls)The booking is listed under Scheduled calls with the status scheduled
6. Ring now — the test ring on the agent's Calls & scheduling page — with the phone lockedThe phone rings on the lock screen: the system's call screen on iPhone, the full-screen call on Android (the call screen)
7. Answer and talk; end the callThe agent knows why it is calling; captions and the timer show; the call ends cleanly
8. Read the outcomes in your listener; tick the in-app call events for your webhook if you want them (outcomes)answered, then ended; a declined or missed test arrives as such
9. Open Call HistoryThe call is there with its transcript and the booking it came from

The QA script repeats these steps with the expected result of each, and the go-live checklist closes the integration.

1.5Questions

Write to support@graine.ai whenever you are blocked; we answer by email, so nothing waits for a meeting. Include the platform and SDK version, the agent's ID (never a secret key or a credential file), what you did, what you expected and what happened, and the SDK's log with debug on. For a call, add its call ID or the booking's ID and the time it happened.

2.What you get

One agent, built and designed in the Graine dashboard, running in your app and on your website — talking, chatting, seeing the screen the customer is on, acting in your app, drawing components, remembering each customer, and calling them the way WhatsApp does.

2.1The agent in your app

  • The assistant bar — a bar drawn by the SDK in your brand's design (chosen in the dashboard, never in code): the agent's avatar, its name and a live status line, the microphone, the hang-up, and a caption card with the line being said. The customer can drag it up or down; it rises above the keyboard.
  • The chat window — typed conversation with the same agent, opened from the bar, with the same screen context, actions and components as voice. The dashboard decides what customers get: a call and a chat, voice only, or chat only.
  • Components drawn on screen — product lists, plan comparisons, info cards, calendar slots, quick actions, lead forms and your own kinds, drawn natively in your design. A tap is the customer's next turn, and your app can be told to open a screen.
  • Screen awareness — your app reports which screen the customer is on, its fields and their state, taps on labelled controls and product events. Personal data (card, account, PAN and Aadhaar numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, plus your own patterns) is masked on the device before anything leaves it.
  • Actions — the agent asks your app to do something you declared (fill a field, open a screen, change a setting) and waits up to six seconds for your handler's answer.

2.2The website widget

The same agent on your website from two script tags: a launcher and a panel with voice and chat, components, and actions on the page — in the same design as your app. It runs in its own frame, so your page's styles cannot reach it and its code cannot reach your page. The page can identify the visitor, describe what they see, and book calls that ring the customer's app.

2.3WhatsApp-style calls, in both directions

  • The customer calls the agent from a button in your app (startCall): the system's call screen on iPhone (CallKit), the SDK's call screen on Android, and the conversation carries on with the screen locked, over Bluetooth, while they use other apps.
  • Graine rings the customer at a booked time — on the lock screen, with the system's incoming-call screen on iPhone and a full-screen call notification on Android. Answered, the call connects to your agent, which knows why it is calling.

Both run on a native call engine inside your app (the platform's audio and echo cancelling). Every outcome — answered, declined, missed, ended, failed — reaches your app; every conversation lands in Call History; and for a call Graine rang, the outcome also updates the booking and reaches your webhooks.

2.4Scheduled calls — booked by the agent, your app or your team

A call can be booked three ways: by the agent during a conversation ("call me back at six"), by your app or website with scheduleCall, or by your team in the dashboard (Schedule a call, or Ring now for a test). Every booking follows the same rules — the agent's Calling Window in the customer's own time zone, quiet hours, how far ahead, how much notice, how many may be waiting — and rings the customer's app.

2.5Memory, and conversations that continue

  • Memory — the agent remembers facts about each customer across conversations, devices and channels (app, website, and phone when the identifier is the phone number), under a one-way key, for the retention you choose. Customers can see what is remembered, turn it off, and erase it from your app.
  • Conversations continue — a returning customer sees the earlier conversation in the chat window and the agent picks up where they left off, like a messaging app: the last 50 messages, kept for 7 days after the last one.

2.6The customer's identifier in Call History

Every in-app and website conversation in Call History shows who it was with — the field your agent identifies people by and its value, for example User ID · u_8812, Email · asha@acme.example or Customer ID · C-20931. The memory service never receives that value: only a one-way key derived from it.

2.7Several agents in one app

One app can run several agents — support in Help, sales on Plans, a coach on Home — each with its own publishable key, design, actions, chat, voice bar and scheduling. They share who the customer is, the device's install, the memory choice and the current screen, and one conversation runs at a time across all of them. Rings are answered by the agent that booked them.

2.8No server of yours

Your app and site integrate with a publishable key (pk_live_…) and the SDKs only. Graine holds the conversation, memory, the bookings, the ringing (with the push credentials you upload once) and the record. The key is public by design: an app request is accepted only when the agent's Allowed domains include app://, a website request only from a listed host, and every route is rate-limited.

3.How it works end to end

3.1The parts and who builds them

PartWhat it doesWhat you write
The SDK, in your appDraws the assistant bar, the chat window, components and the call screen in your design; masks personal data before anything leaves the phone; keeps the install ID; runs the voice engine and the native call engine; registers the device for rings and reports every call outcome. A few lines at launch, identify() at sign-in, one screen report per screen, one handler per action, and — for calls — two lines that hand the SDK its push tokens.
The loader, on your websiteDraws the launcher and the panel (an isolated frame) in the same design; voice, chat, components and actions on the page.Two script tags; optionally identify(), setScreen() and defineAction().
GraineRuns the agent, keeps memory and the recent conversation under a one-way key, holds the bookings and rings the customer with your credentials, records every conversation in Call History, sends your webhooks. Nothing — settings in the dashboard.
Apple and Google pushDeliver the ring (an APNs VoIP push; a high-priority FCM data message). Upload an APNs auth key and a Firebase service account once (Workspace settings → In-app calling).
Your systems (optional)Receive webhooks; serve live data for components; run the agent's tools. Only if you want them.

Two engines, one agent

  • The voice engine carries the assistant bar's voice. Every SDK hosts the same engine, loaded from Graine into a small invisible web view the SDK owns, so an audio fix reaches your app without a release. Its audio goes over the high-quality path (WebRTC) when the agent's Call audio is set to it, falling back to the standard path when it cannot connect. The chat has its own connection.
  • The native call engine carries WhatsApp-style calls. Its audio runs in your app's own process with the platform's echo canceller, which is what lets a call ring through CallKit and keep going with the screen off. It improves when you update the SDK.
  • One conversation at a time. Starting a native call ends a conversation in the bar; the bar does not start while a call is live; and with several agents, starting a conversation on one ends a live one on another.

Your app passes nothing about how the agent looks. The SDK reads the design from the agent's settings once per launch, so a design saved in the dashboard reaches a website on its next page load and an app the next time it starts. The last design is kept on the device, so a ring that wakes a closed app is drawn in your brand.

3.2A session starts, with identity

  1. Session. Once per launch the SDK fetches the agent's settings with the publishable key: the design, the declared actions, which trait identifies a customer (Who is the user?), whether memory is on, the scheduling rules and the call settings. The last one is kept on the device for a cold start.
  2. Identify. After sign-in your app calls identify(traits, memory). The trait the agent's Who is the user? setting names (user_id unless you chose another) is the identifier: it is kept as it is and never becomes a prompt variable. Every other trait is masked on the device and becomes a prompt variable ({name}, {plan}). Calling it before the session has arrived is fine.
  3. A conversation starts (a chat, the bar's voice, or a native call). The SDK asks Graine for a single-use connection ticket that is valid for two minutes, sending the install ID, the identifier, the customer's memory choice, the device's time zone and, for a call, its call ID.
  4. Graine checks the key and the agent's Allowed domains (an app needs app://), turns the identifier into a one-way user key, and checks that this install is one of the customer's allowed devices (Devices per user).
  5. The conversation opens on the agent, with the customer's prompt variables. Memory is recalled only when the agent remembers, the customer has not opted out, and the device is one of theirs; recall is given 1.5 seconds and the conversation goes ahead without it rather than wait.
  6. While it runs, the SDK sends the screen as it changes (masked, numbered, the first change at once and later ones at most every 400 ms), taps on labelled controls, and the answers to the agent's action requests.

Identity is fixed for a conversation when it starts: a sign-in during a conversation applies to the next one.

3.3A chat, with memory and continuation

  • Memory holds long-term facts ("prefers a call after 6 pm"). The agent recalls them once when a conversation starts — every kind of agent, every step of a flow — and new facts are stored in the background as the conversation goes and when it ends, so allow a short while before a new fact can be recalled.
  • Continuation holds the recent conversation itself: the last 50 messages per agent and customer, for 7 days after the last one. A new chat starts from them — the chat window shows the earlier messages and the agent continues; no welcome message is repeated. Conversations continue has the details.
  • Both apply only to an identified customer, on a device that is one of theirs, on an agent with memory on, who has not opted out. Anyone else gets nothing kept and nothing restored — never a shared bucket.

3.4The customer calls the agent

  1. Your call button calls startCall(reason). It returns the call's ID (call_ and a lowercase UUID), or nothing while another call is live.
  2. The SDK asks for the microphone if the app does not have it, places the call — a CallKit call on iPhone, the SDK's call screen on Android — and connects to the agent with who_called = "customer", call_reason set to your reason, your call variables, the customer's identity and the current screen. A conversation in the bar ends first.
  3. The call goes on with the screen locked, in another app, or on a Bluetooth headset. The agent can still run your actions.
  4. When it ends, your app hears the outcome — ended with local (the customer hung up), remote (the agent did) or failed (the line broke; calls do not reconnect) — and the conversation is in Call History.

3.5A booked call rings the customer's phone

  1. When the time comes, Graine checks that the call may ring now: credit and the agent being on; the agent's Calling Window in the customer's own time zone; quiet hours for calls the agent or your team booked; no ring within 6 hours of a decline; the daily ring limit; and a device to ring (seen in the last 30 days).
  2. The ring goes to the customer's newest device through APNs (a VoIP push) or FCM (a high-priority data message). It carries the call's ID, the call name and which agent is calling — no reason, no variables, nothing about the customer.
  3. The SDK rings. On iPhone it reports the call to CallKit at once — iOS requires every VoIP push to be reported, and the SDK reports every one. On Android it posts a call notification that fills a locked screen. It tells Graine the phone is ringing.
  4. The customer answers on the lock screen or in your app. The SDK reports answered and opens the conversation with the call's ID; the agent receives the booking's reason (as call_reason) and variables, and the customer's memory.
  5. The outcome — ended with its duration, or declined, missed or failed — goes to your app and to Graine, which updates the scheduled call, files the conversation in Call History and sends your webhooks (call_declined, call_missed, call_expired). A missed ring can ring once more after the delay you set; a declined one never rings again.

3.6Three ways to book

Booked byHowNeeds (Calls & scheduling)Quiet hours apply?
The agentDuring a conversation, when the customer asks to be called backThe agent, during a conversationYes
Your app or websitescheduleCall(at, reason)Users, from your appNo — a time the customer picked is theirs to keep
Your teamAgent → Calls & scheduling → Schedule a call; Ring now for a testPush credentials uploadedYes

Every booking must fall inside the agent's Calling Window in the customer's time zone, and is refused at booking time if it does not. On a phone call, the agent's booking is an ordinary call back to the caller's number.

4.Agent types: prompt agents and flow agents

Both kinds of agent use the same voices, languages, knowledge base, webhooks and widgets, and both go into your app and onto your website the same way — the SDKs do not change. They differ in how the conversation is written.

Prompt agentFlow agent
Made ofOne prompt that covers the whole conversationA briefing every step shares, plus steps that each carry their own instructions, joined by paths
Each turn, the model readsThe whole promptThe briefing and the current step only, so a long script stays focused
Choose it forOpen conversations where the order does not matter: support questions, FAQs, discoveryA conversation with a shape it must keep: confirm who you are speaking to, check something, agree a date, say goodbye
Created fromSidebar Build → Agents → New agentSidebar Build → Flow agents → New flow agent, or Convert to a flow agent in a prompt agent's editor (it drafts steps and creates a new agent; the original is unchanged)

4.1How a flow agent is built

  • Steps. AI reply — the AI talks, following the step's instructions on top of the briefing; it can read the knowledge base and use tools, and it is the only kind of step that can end the conversation. Fixed line — says the same line every time, word for word, in the caller's language. Branch — says nothing; it checks its paths and moves on within the same turn.
  • Paths. AI decides, Rule, Always (the fallback) and Event. Rules are checked first, then the model's decision, then Always; otherwise the conversation stays on its step. The customer always hears the step they have just been moved to.
  • Test and publish. The builder's Test area runs a chat, a web call or a phone call against the agent as saved. A new flow agent is a draft until Go live.

4.2Flow agents in your app and on your website

In your app and on your websiteOn a phone call
Which agent answersThe agent's web-call variant, kept in step with every saveThe agent itself
ComponentsOffered on every AI reply step (say in the step's instructions when to show one); a choice in a component arrives as the customer's next turn, so a path can branch on it. A step set to Uses a tool cannot be a componentNone — write such steps so they also work by voice
Screen context and in-app actionsEvery AI reply step knows which screen the customer is on and which component is open, and can call your actionsNone
MemoryRecalled once when the conversation starts, and reaching every stepThe same, keyed on the caller's number
Fixed linesSaid word for word and captioned; in a chat they arrive as textSaid word for word
Your systems moving the conversation (events)Not availableEvent paths, through the API

For a flow agent, Embed & Widgets sits in the flow builder's header and shows Install, Appearance, Actions, On screen and Friction; its Users & memory and Calls settings are reached through All settings, which opens the agent editor. Embed settings save on their own, not with the flow's Save.

One agent per surface.

Actions are declared on the agent, and the model is offered every one of them on every surface that agent serves. Give your app its own agent — clone it from your existing one (the agent editor's More actions menu → Clone this agent) so the prompt and knowledge base come across — and change only what differs. A clone starts without the original's embed and widgets.

5.Dashboard setup, step by step

Everything below is in the Graine dashboard at https://www.graine.ai. Labels are written exactly as the dashboard shows them. An agent's settings are under Build → Agents → the agent → the Configuration panel, whose sections include Embed & Widgets, Memory, Calling Window, Calls & scheduling, Custom Variables and Integrations & Tools. Workspace-wide settings are under Account → Workspace settings.

#WhereWhat you setWho
1Build → AgentsAn agent for the app (clone your existing agent) and one for the websiteAgent editors
2Agent → Embed & Widgets → InstallSet up embedding; copy the publishable key; Allowed domains: app:// for the app, your hosts for the websiteA role that manages integrations
3Embed & Widgets → AppearanceThe design in the Garage (Assistant bar, Chat window, Call screen) and the Setup cardAgent editors
4Actions, On screen, FrictionWhat the agent may do in your app, the components it may draw, when it speaks up firstAgent editors
5Agent → Memory (also Embed & Widgets → Users & memory)Memory on, Who is the user?, Devices per user, what is remembered and for how longAgent editors
6Agent → Calls & scheduling (also Embed & Widgets → Calls)Who may book, the call name, ringing rules, quiet hours; booked callsAgent editors; placing a call needs permission to place calls
7Account → Workspace settings → In-app callingAPNs key and Firebase service account, until each shows VerifiedAn Admin (manages integrations)
8The agent's promptUse {who_called} and {call_reason}; when to offer a call backAgent editors

5.1Embed & Widgets → Install: the key and Allowed domains

  1. Open the agent → Embed & Widgets. If it shows Not set up for the web yet, press Set up embedding: it creates the agent's publishable key (pk_live_…). The status strip then reads Ready to embed (or No domains yet).
  2. Publishable key — copy it into your app's configuration and your website snippet. It identifies the agent and is public by design. Rotate key issues a new one; every page and build still using the old key stops working immediately, with no grace period — ship the new key first.
  3. Allowed domains — Only these domains can load this agent. Add several at once with commas. Use .example.com to include subdomains, and app:// for your mobile app.
    • For your app, add app:// (typing app or app://* saves the same entry). A native app sends no browser origin; Graine refuses such requests unless app:// is listed, with the error This agent does not accept requests from a mobile app yet. Add "app://" to its Allowed domains under Agent → Embed & Widgets. The entry lets in any app that holds the key: treat the key as public; rate limits and single-use connection tickets bound it.
    • For your website, add every host exactly, staging included: example.com does not cover www.example.com. An empty list refuses every site. A page on localhost is refused like any other site: add localhost to the list while you test from your machine, and remove it before you go live.
  4. The Website | Mobile app switch shows a ready snippet with your agent ID and key filled in (Mobile app shows React Native; the other platforms are in Install and set up, per platform).

5.2Embed & Widgets → Appearance: the Garage and Setup

Colour, logo and layout. Changes reach every site and app running this agent — the snippet does not change. The Garage is a showroom of designs (Garage · 23 designs); pick one, tune it under Make it yours (Paint, Body, Typeface, Rims, Lights, Interior, Chat, Call), preview it as In-app or Website on an iPhone or Android, and Save design. The footer then reads Saved — live on every site and app.

Garage tabControls (Tuning → the matching category)
Assistant barThe bar's look comes from the design and its tuning: colours (Accent, Neutral tone, Light or dark), typeface, corners, depth, motion.
Chat window (moments New chat, Conversation, Returning customer)Title and subtitle (title up to 40 characters, subtitle up to 60, default Online); Avatar: Logo / Glyph / None; Header: Surface / Accent; Background: Plain / Tint / Pattern; Starters — up to 4, each up to 40 characters, sent exactly as written when tapped; Composer → Placeholder (default Message…); Timestamps: Hidden / Shown.
Window size: Compact · Large · Full screen — How big the chat opens on a phone. On a tablet or computer, Large and Full screen open a panel.
New conversation button: Shown / Hidden — The compose button in the header that starts a fresh conversation. It shows while earlier messages are on screen. Hidden, there is no control; newConversation() still works from a button of yours.
Booked calls: Shown / Hidden, and Card title (empty: "Upcoming call" / "Upcoming calls") — the card of the customer's upcoming calls at the top of the chat, each with Cancel. The iOS, Android, Flutter and Kotlin Multiplatform SDKs draw it; React Native's chat and the website have no booked-calls card, so this control changes nothing there.
Earlier messages: Shown / Hidden — A customer who comes back sees the conversation from before. Hidden, the chat opens empty, like a new one, and your assistant still remembers it.
These save in the design as chat.showUpcomingCalls, chat.upcomingTitle, chat.showHistory and chat.newConversation; the SDKs read them into their chat tokens (iOS GraineChatTokens).
Call screen (moments Scheduled, Ringing, Connecting, On call, Ended, Missed)Background: Brand / Dark / Light / Accent / Gradient; Avatar: Logo / Glyph / Letter; Avatar shape: Circle / Squircle / Rounded; End button: Round / Pill; Buttons on a call: Mute, Speaker, Chat, End (which and in what order; End is always there); Captions: Shown / Hidden; Timer: Shown / Hidden; Ringtone: Phone's own / Graine / Soft; Words for each moment: Scheduled call ringing (default "Scheduled call"), Other call ringing ("Incoming call"), Connecting ("Connecting…"), Ended ("Call ended"), Missed ("Missed call"), up to 40 characters each.

Setup (under the design, saved on its own with Save setup): What visitors get — Call and chat / Voice only / Chat only; Opens on — Call / Chat; Corner (websites only); Heading (default "Talk to our AI assistant"); Launcher tooltip (websites only, default "Chat with us"); Call audio — Standard / High quality (WebRTC); Logo; Background behind the logo; Show “Powered by Graine AI”; and Loading (the loader and its words while connecting, reconnecting, thinking and loading a component). Native apps use What visitors get, Opens on, Heading, Logo, Loading and Call audio from here, and the whole design above.

The call screen names the call with Calls & scheduling → Name on the incoming call — on the phone and in the Garage's preview alike (the Appearance Heading when it is not set).

5.3Actions, On screen and Friction

  • Actions — What this agent may do in your app. Each action has a Tool name, When should the agent use this? and Arguments; ready-made ones are Navigate, Fill a field, Highlight, Retry and Blank. Save and sync to agent pushes them to the agent at once. Your app must implement a handler with the same name — declaring it here does not create the behaviour, it creates the contract.
  • On screen — What this agent can put on screen: tick the components (built in the dashboard's components editor) and Save selection.
  • Friction — When the agent should notice someone is stuck: Friction detection on or off; rules Idle on a step, Same field rejecting them, Going back and forth, Rage taps, Moving on with something missing, Error banner; per-screen overrides; How often it may speak up; Open the assistant when nobody is talking to it.

5.4Agent → Memory: People and Settings

Remembers users across chats and calls. The agent recognises a returning person — in your app, on your website or on the phone — and picks up where they left off. What it remembers about one person is never used with anyone else. The identifier your app sends is shown in Call History beside each conversation. The same screen is the Users & memory tab of Embed & Widgets. It has two tabs, People and Settings.

Settings

SettingChoicesWhat it does
Remembers users across chats and callsOn / offOn: in your app, on your website and on phone calls, the agent recalls what it learned about the user before. Off: every conversation starts fresh.
Who is the user?User ID (default) · Email · Phone number · Custom field (with Field name, for example patient_id, member_number or customer_id)The trait your app's identify() must carry: user_id, email, phone or your field's name. The agent remembers each value as one person, scheduled calls ring that person, and Call History shows it. Phone calls: always the caller's number. The setting below is for your app and website. Changing it starts every app user fresh.
Devices per user1–5 (default 2)How many phones or browsers can act as the same user at once. A device beyond this still works, but without that user's memory and scheduled calls — until another is signed out or reset below.
Shared withThis agent only · Agents that share memoryWhether what this agent learns is recalled by other agents in the workspace that also share memory.
Keep memories for30 days, 90 days, 180 days, 1 year (default), 2 years, or another number of daysA memory older than this is deleted. Deleting the agent does not delete its memories early.
What to remember — and what never toUp to 1,000 charactersInstructions for what is kept and what never is (for example: never card numbers).

Two buttons save these: Save (the identity settings) and Save memory settings.

People, and a person's panel

  • People lists People … has talked to (the newest 1,000 conversations), searchable by name or identifier. Each row shows <field label> · <value> (for example User ID · u_8812), the name, the number of conversations and the last one, and channel chips Chat, Voice, In-app call, Phone. Find a person looks someone up by identifier (App user) or by number (Caller).
  • The person's panel shows What … remembers about this person, each memory with Learned/Updated and Delete this memory; their recent conversations; and two buttons: Forget this person (Everything this agent remembers about them is deleted, now. Their next conversation starts fresh. This can't be undone.) and Reset devices (Every phone and browser signed in as them stops acting as them until they sign in again. Use this when someone changed phones and hit the device limit.). The panel does not list the devices themselves.

5.5Agent → Calls & scheduling

Graine can ring this agent's users inside your app — full screen, like a phone call — at a time the agent, the user or your team booked. Calls keep to this agent's Calling Window in the user's own time zone. The same screen is the Calls tab of Embed & Widgets. Set the agent's hours under Calling Window first.

SettingDefaultRangeWhat it does
Who may book a call
The agent, during a conversationOffOn / offWhen a user asks to be called back, the agent books it for the time they pick — in the app, the user is rung there; on a phone call, the number is called back.
Users, from your appOffOn / offYour app (or website) may call scheduleCall. A time a user picks is checked against the Calling Window when they book.
At most this many upcoming calls per user3 calls1–10Pending bookings per customer (maxPendingPerUser).
Booked at most this far ahead14 days1–30The furthest ahead (maxDaysAhead).
With at least this much notice5 minutes2–1440The soonest (minLeadMinutes).
How it rings
Name on the incoming callThe agent's nameUp to 40 charactersWhat the user's phone shows when it rings.
Ring for45 seconds20–60How long a ring lasts before it is missed.
After a missed call, ring once more after10 minutes0–120One re-ring after a miss; 0 never rings again. A declined call is never rung again.
Ring each user at most3 times a day1–10Rings per customer per day, in their own day.
Quiet hoursOn, 21:00 to 08:00From / toCalls the agent or your team book never ring in these hours, in the user's own time zone. A time the user picked themselves is theirs to keep.

Save with Save call settings. Above the settings, The call screen previews the ring, the call and a missed call from the saved design, and the card Your app's push credentials shows the workspace's credentials (below).

  • Schedule a call (a form on the page): App user or Phone number; the identifier (labelled with your Who is the user? field, for example User ID — The user is rung on the devices they're signed in on.); Label (optional); When; Time zone (The time above is read in this zone); What it's about (optional) — The agent is told when the call starts. It never appears on the user's phone. Press Schedule call.
  • Ring a user now → Ring now: A test: rings this user's phone right away with the screen above, and shows what happened. It follows every booking rule except the notice period (a test outside the Calling Window or quiet hours is refused), counts toward that user's rings for the day, and appears in the list as Test ring.
  • Scheduled calls lists bookings (Find calls for a … by identifier, Show all, Refresh): who, "… their time (zone) · … your time", who booked it (Booked by the agent, Booked by the app, Booked by Dashboard, Booked by API) and a status chip: Upcoming, Ringing, Answered, Completed, Declined, Missed, Failed, Cancelled, Too late to ring (expired), No device to ring. Cancel appears while a call is Upcoming (Cancel this call? → Cancel call).

5.6Workspace settings → In-app calling (push credentials)

Let Graine ring your app's users for scheduled calls — full screen, like a phone call, inside your app. Add your app's push credentials once; agents then choose who may book calls under Calls & scheduling. One card per platform; each shows Not set up, Verified, Not working (with the last error) or Not checked yet.

CardFieldsWhere to get them
iOSBundle ID; Team ID and Key ID (10 letters and digits each); Environment: Automatic (each device's own), Production (App Store and TestFlight), Sandbox (development builds); Push key (.p8 file)Apple Developer account → Keys → a key with Apple Push Notifications enabled (download the .p8 once; note its Key ID). Your Team ID is on your membership page.
AndroidPackage name; Service-account key (.json file)Firebase console → Project settings → Service accounts → Generate new private key (a service account allowed to send messages for that project).

Press Set up (or Replace), choose the file, and Save and check. Graine checks without ringing anyone: on iOS it sends a push on your app's VoIP topic to a device token that does not exist — Apple answers "bad device token" when the key and topic are good, and refuses the key when not; on Android it sends a validate-only message. The credentials are stored encrypted and never shown again. Remove stops all ringing for that platform at once. If Apple or Google later refuses the credentials when a ring is sent, the card turns Not working and your admins get one notification in the dashboard.

5.7The prompt: who_called and call_reason

For every native call the agent receives two prompt variables (they are not shown in the dashboard; use them in the prompt):

VariableValues
who_calledcustomer — the customer placed the call from your app; agent — a ring your own push server sent; scheduled — a call Graine rang (a booked call), on every platform, and a phone call-back the agent booked. Treat agent and scheduled alike: your side rang the customer.
call_reasonThe reason: what your app passed to startCall, or the booking's What it's about / reason. Left out when there is none.

A variable nothing sets is left out of the prompt, so write the prompt to read well without it:

Prompt (example)
If {who_called} is "agent" or "scheduled", you are calling the customer: greet them by name, say you are
calling from Acme, and ask whether now is a good time. The reason for the call, if there is one: {call_reason}.
If {who_called} is "customer", they called you: ask how you can help.

Other variables come from identify() traits (masked; never the identifier), setVariables(), the call's own variables and the agent's Custom Variables. A conversation carries up to 12 variables, about 1 KB in all.

6.Install and set up, per platform

Each platform below has the same parts: requirements, install, size, permissions and capabilities (word for word), what the SDK asks for at run time, store declarations, and the code that starts it. One rule holds everywhere: the SDK asks for the microphone and nothing else, and only when a conversation or a call starts without it. Everything else is declared by your app at build time; the notification permission Android needs for rings is yours to ask for.

6.2React Native

Packages@graineai/inapp-react-native 0.41.0 (the agent) · @graineai/inapp-react-native-calls 0.2.0 (native calls, optional)
RequiresThe SDK: React Native 0.68+ and React 17+ (its peer dependencies), plus react-native-webview (the voice engine runs in it). The calls package: React Native 0.71+, React 18+, a native build (not Expo Go), iOS 15+ (its pod) and Android 7 / API 24+ (its Gradle module, Java 17). Node 18+ for development.
Recommendedexpo-font (passed as loadFont: the SDK then loads the design's typeface) and react-native-svg (passed as svg: icons in the design's style). Without them: the system font and plain glyphs.
ExpoA development build (SDK 50+). Expo Go cannot load react-native-webview or the calls package. Neither package ships an Expo config plugin: put the settings in app.json (below).
Install
npm install @graineai/inapp-react-native react-native-webview
npm install @graineai/inapp-react-native-calls      # native calls (optional)
npm install expo-font react-native-svg              # the design's typeface and icons (recommended)
cd ios && pod install

Permissions and capabilities

  • The SDK package carries no manifest. Declare the microphone yourself: Android RECORD_AUDIO and MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS; iOS NSMicrophoneUsageDescription.
  • The calls package's Android manifest merges everything a call needs — the same list as the Android SDK (microphone, notifications, full-screen ring, microphone foreground service, the call screen, its service and receiver). On iOS, add the capabilities and the usage string from the iOS section: Push Notifications, Background Modes → Audio and Voice over IP.
  • At run time: on Android the SDK asks for the microphone when a call starts; on iOS the system asks the first time the microphone is used. The calls package asks for the microphone before it places or answers a call. Notifications on Android 13+ are yours to ask for (POST_NOTIFICATIONS) — without them a ring cannot show while your app is closed.
  • iPhone ringer switch: the SDK leaves the app's audio session to you for the bar's voice — while a conversation is live, set your audio library's equivalents of playsInSilentModeIOS: true and allowsRecordingIOS: true, or the agent is silent when the ringer is off. (Native calls set their own session.)
JSONapp.json (Expo)
{
  "expo": {
    "ios": {
      "infoPlist": {
        "NSMicrophoneUsageDescription": "Lets you talk to the assistant in the app and on calls.",
        "UIBackgroundModes": ["audio", "voip"]
      },
      "entitlements": { "aps-environment": "production" }
    },
    "android": {
      "permissions": ["android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO", "android.permission.MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS"]
    }
  }
}

aps-environment is the Push Notifications capability: development for development builds, production for TestFlight and App Store builds. With the calls package installed, its manifest adds the Android entries at build time anyway.

Initialise

React Native · TypeScriptApp.tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { WebView } from "react-native-webview";
import * as Font from "expo-font";
import Svg, { Path } from "react-native-svg";
import {
  GraineProvider, GraineVoiceLauncher, GraineVoiceBar, GraineLauncherButton, useGraineClient,
} from "@graineai/inapp-react-native";
import { GraineCalls } from "@graineai/inapp-react-native-calls";

export default function App() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <GraineProvider
      baseUrl="https://www.graine.ai"
      publishableKey="pk_live_…"            // Agent → Embed & Widgets → Install
      navigationRef={navigationRef}         // the same ref as your NavigationContainer: screens are reported for you
      loadFont={Font.loadAsync}
      svg={{ Svg, Path }}
    >
      <NavigationContainer ref={navigationRef}><RootNavigator /></NavigationContainer>
      <GraineVoiceLauncher webView={WebView} active={open} autoStart>
        {(api) => (open ? <GraineVoiceBar api={api} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} /> : null)}
      </GraineVoiceLauncher>
      {!open && <GraineLauncherButton onPress={() => setOpen(true)} style={{ position: "absolute", right: 16, bottom: 24 }} />}
      <CallsBridge />
    </GraineProvider>
  );
}

// Native calls: configure once and hand the call what the app tells the agent.
function CallsBridge() {
  const client = useGraineClient();
  useEffect(() => {
    GraineCalls.configure({ publishableKey: "pk_live_…", displayName: "Asha from Acme" });
    return GraineCalls.attach(client);      // identity, variables, the screen and your actions reach the call
  }, [client]);
  return null;
}

GraineVoiceLauncher owns the engine and the call; mounted early with active={false} it loads the engine before the tap. GraineVoiceBar draws the bar, the chat window (where the agent offers chat) and components, in the dashboard's design.

6.3iOS (Swift)

PackageGraineInApp 0.7.0 — a Swift package with no dependencies
RequiresiOS 15+ (Mac Catalyst 15+ also builds); Swift tools 5.9 (Xcode 15 or later). It links Apple's AVFoundation, CallKit, Combine, CoreGraphics, CoreText, PushKit, SwiftUI, UIKit and WebKit.
Calls needA real iPhone (CallKit and VoIP pushes do not run in the simulator), an Apple Developer account and an APNs auth key for hosted ringing

Install — Swift Package Manager (primary)

Xcode → File → Add Package Dependencies… → https://github.com/GraineAI/inapp-ios, version 0.7.0 or later, and add the GraineInApp library to your app target. In a Package.swift:

Package.swift
dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/GraineAI/inapp-ios", from: "0.7.0"),
],
targets: [
    .target(name: "AcmeApp", dependencies: [.product(name: "GraineInApp", package: "inapp-ios")]),
]

Install — CocoaPods

CocoaPodsPodfile
platform :ios, '15.0'
target 'AcmeApp' do
  use_frameworks!
  pod 'GraineInApp', '~> 0.7'
  # or straight from the tag:
  # pod 'GraineInApp', :git => 'https://github.com/GraineAI/inapp-ios.git', :tag => '0.7.0'
end

The pod builds exactly what the Swift package builds (the same sources, iOS 15, Swift 5.9) and carries the privacy manifest in its own resource bundle, GraineInApp_Privacy.

Permissions and capabilities

Add (Xcode → the app target)ForWhy
NSMicrophoneUsageDescription in Info.plistVoice and callsRequired: iOS stops an app that asks for the microphone without it. Suggested text: Lets you talk to the assistant in the app and on calls.
Signing & Capabilities → Push NotificationsCalls that ringVoIP pushes reach the app (the aps-environment entitlement)
Background Modes → Audio, AirPlay, and Picture in Picture (audio)CallsThe call's audio keeps going with the screen off
Background Modes → Voice over IP (voip)Calls that ringiOS wakes a closed app for a VoIP push
XMLInfo.plist
<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>Lets you talk to the assistant in the app and on calls.</string>
<key>UIBackgroundModes</key>
<array>
    <string>audio</string>
    <string>voip</string>
</array>

Nothing else: no notification permission (VoIP pushes and CallKit need none), no Bluetooth usage description, no remote-notification background mode. The SDK ships a privacy manifest declaring the required-reason APIs it calls — system boot time (reason 35F9.1, for timing) and UserDefaults (reason CA92.1) — and no tracking and no tracking domains; Xcode adds it to your app's privacy report. What your app collects through the agent, the customer's voice included, goes in your App Privacy details.

What the SDK configures in CallKit

CallKit settingValue
Call name (caller on the system screen, Recents)For a ring Graine sends: the agent's Name on the incoming call (else the agent's name). For a call the customer places, and a ring from your own server without a name: GraineCallsConfig.displayName; with several agents, each agent's call name first; empty, your app's display name.
Icon template (the app button on the system call screen)GraineCallsConfig.iconTemplateImageData (a 40 × 40 pt transparent PNG); otherwise the brand's launcher glyph from the design, drawn as a template image
RingtoneGraineCallsConfig.ringtoneSound (a sound file in your bundle, 30 seconds or less); otherwise the Garage's Ringtone — Graine or Soft written as a sound file for CallKit, or the phone's own ringtone for Phone's own
Calls in the Phone app's RecentsGraineCallsConfig.includesCallsInRecents, off by default
Video, hold, grouping, keypadOff: voice only, one call at a time (one call group, one call per group)
Ring timeoutA ring Graine sends rings for the agent's Ring for; any other for GraineCallsConfig.ringTimeout (30 seconds by default)
Audio sessionPlay-and-record in voice-chat mode, Bluetooth hands-free allowed, the earpiece by default; activated by CallKit, and the app's own session restored afterwards
  • Every VoIP push is reported to CallKit at once. iOS requires it and stops delivering VoIP pushes to an app that does not. The SDK reports every one — even one it cannot use, or one that arrives during a live call (that one is ended at once and reported missed; the live call is untouched). Send VoIP pushes only for calls. An app with its own PKPushRegistry hands the payload to reportIncomingCall(payload:completion:) instead.
  • On the lock screen the ring is the system's incoming-call screen (a banner while the phone is in use), with your call name, icon and ringtone. Answered there, the call connects; the system call screen stays on the lock screen for the call, and your app shows GraineCallView when it is opened. Do Not Disturb, a Focus or the block list can stop a ring; it is then reported missed.
  • The microphone: for a call the customer places, the SDK asks before placing it. For a ring, the customer answers first; the SDK reports answered, iOS asks while the call connects, and a refusal — or no answer within 60 seconds — ends it failed. Ask during onboarding so a call answered on the lock screen already has it.
  • Apple does not allow CallKit in apps on the App Store in China: leave calls off there.

Initialise

iOS · SwiftAcmeApp.swift
import SwiftUI
import GraineInApp

@main
struct AcmeApp: App {
    @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor(AppDelegate.self) private var appDelegate
    var body: some Scene { WindowGroup { RootView() } }
}

final class AppDelegate: NSObject, UIApplicationDelegate {
    func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                     didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]? = nil) -> Bool {
        let graine = GraineInApp.configure(GraineConfig(
            baseUrl: "https://www.graine.ai",
            publishableKey: "pk_live_…",          // Agent → Embed & Widgets → Install
            appVersion: "2.4.0"
        ))
        graine.calls.configure(GraineCallsConfig(displayName: "Asha from Acme"))
        graine.calls.enableVoIPPushes()           // every launch: iOS hands over a VoIP push only once this has run
        return true
    }
}

struct RootView: View {
    @ObservedObject private var calls = GraineInApp.shared.calls
    var body: some View {
        AppContent()
            .overlay(GraineAgentBar())            // the bar: voice, chat and components, in your design
            .fullScreenCover(isPresented: .constant(calls.showsCallScreen)) {
                GraineCallView()                  // the call while your app is open
            }
    }
}

The bar mounts the voice engine in the key window the first time it appears (autoAttach), so a call carries on as the customer moves through your app. UIKit apps host the SwiftUI views in a UIHostingController, or use GraineChatViewController; without the bar, mount the engine with GraineInApp.shared.voice.attach().

What the library's manifest merges into your app

EntryWhy
android.permission.INTERNETThe voice engine and the conversation's connection
android.permission.RECORD_AUDIOThe agent hears the customer (voice and calls). A runtime permission: the SDK asks
android.permission.MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGSA call routes its audio — earpiece, loudspeaker or a headset, Bluetooth included (no Bluetooth permission is needed)
android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONSThe ring, the ongoing call and a missed call are notifications. A runtime permission on Android 13+: your app asks
android.permission.USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENTA ring that fills a locked screen. On Android 14+ Google Play grants it by default only to apps whose main purpose is calling or alarms; without it the ring is a heads-up notification, still ringing
android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICEThe call runs in a foreground service
android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONEThat service keeps the microphone with the screen off (type microphone)
ai.graine.inapp.GraineCallActivityThe call screen: its own task (so ending a call returns the customer to where they were), shown over the lock screen, not exported
ai.graine.inapp.GraineChatActivityThe chat on a screen of its own (GraineChatActivity.open), above the keyboard; not exported
ai.graine.inapp.GraineCallServiceThe call's foreground service, foregroundServiceType="microphone", not exported
ai.graine.inapp.GraineCallReceiverThe notifications' Decline and Hang up, not exported

What the SDK asks at run time: only RECORD_AUDIO — at voice.start() for the bar (forward your activity's onRequestPermissionsResult to voice.onRequestPermissionsResult), and from the call screen when a call is placed or after Answer (a refusal ends the call failed; no answer within 60 seconds too). Your app asks for notifications on Android 13+; without them, a ring with your app closed or in the background cannot show and ends missed. Your app offers the full-screen setting on Android 14+:

Android · Kotlin — onboarding
private val ask = registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions()) { }

fun askForAgentPermissions() {
    val wanted = mutableListOf(Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO)
    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33) wanted += Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS   // rings
    ask.launch(wanted.toTypedArray())
}

fun offerFullScreenRings() {
    val nm = getSystemService(NotificationManager::class.java)
    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 34 && !nm.canUseFullScreenIntent()) {
        startActivity(Intent(Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_APP_USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT, Uri.parse("package:$packageName")))
    }
}

Notification channels the SDK creates in calls.configure (visible in the phone's settings): Incoming calls (high importance, the ringtone, vibration, shown on the lock screen), Incoming calls (app ringtone) (used while the SDK plays the brand's Graine or Soft ring), Missed calls and Ongoing calls.

The ring is a call-style notification (Android 12+; Decline and Answer actions before that) that keeps ringing until answered, declined or timed out, with a full-screen intent to the call screen; when your app is in front, the call screen opens straight away. The call runs in the microphone foreground service with an ongoing notification (On a call / Connecting…, a timer, Hang up). A ring nobody answered leaves a Missed calls notification with Call back.

Not using calls? On Android 14+, Google Play asks apps that declare USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT or FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE to justify them. An app that never places or receives calls removes them in its own manifest:

XMLAndroidManifest.xml (an app without calls)
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools">
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT" tools:node="remove" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE" tools:node="remove" />
    <application>
        <service android:name="ai.graine.inapp.GraineCallService" tools:node="remove" />
    </application>
</manifest>

6.8Store review

StoreWhat to declare
App StoreReview notes: say the app offers voice calls with your assistant; give the reviewer a test account and where the call button is; explain that agent calls ring through VoIP pushes your backend (or Graine) sends, which the reviewer cannot trigger. VoIP: pushes are used only for calls, and every one is reported to CallKit. Privacy: the microphone purpose string; App Privacy details for the audio and data your app sends through the agent; the SDK's privacy manifest covers its required-reason APIs. China: no CallKit on the China storefront.
Google PlayForeground service permissions (App content): the call's service is type microphone — describe two-way voice calls with your assistant that keep going when the screen locks, with a short video. Full-screen intent: declare it (granted by default only to calling and alarm apps) or go without; rings are then heads-up notifications. Data safety: the audio and data your app sends for the conversation.

7.Identity and memory

Memory, conversations that continue and calls that ring a customer all need to know who the customer is. On a phone call it is always the phone number. In your app and on your website it is the trait the agent's Who is the user? setting names (Agent → Memory → Settings): user_id by default, or email, phone, or a field of your own such as customer_id. Your app passes it with identify().

7.1identify(…) after sign-in, identify(null) on sign-out

React Native · TypeScript
const identify = useGraineIdentify();
useEffect(() => {
  identify(user ? { user_id: user.id, name: user.firstName, plan: user.plan } : null, { memory: user?.allowsMemory ?? true });
}, [user]);
// outside React: client.identify({ user_id: user.id, name: user.firstName }); client.identify(null);
iOS · Swift
GraineInApp.shared.identify(["user_id": user.id, "name": user.firstName, "plan": user.plan], memory: user.allowsMemory)
// on sign-out, and before another customer signs in
GraineInApp.shared.identify(nil)
Android · Kotlin
GraineInApp.get().identify(mapOf("user_id" to user.id, "name" to user.firstName, "plan" to user.plan), memory = user.allowsMemory)
// on sign-out
GraineInApp.get().identify(null)
Flutter · Dart
GraineInApp.instance.identify({'user_id': user.id, 'name': user.firstName, 'plan': user.plan}, memory: user.allowsMemory);
// on sign-out
GraineInApp.instance.identify(null);
Kotlin Multiplatform · Kotlin
Graine.identify(mapOf("user_id" to user.id, "name" to user.firstName), memory = user.allowsMemory)
Graine.identify(null)                                    // sign out
Website · JavaScript
GraineAgent.identify({ user_id: user.id, name: user.firstName }, { memory: user.allowsMemory });
GraineAgent.identify(null);                              // on sign-out: every agent on the page
TraitMasked on the deviceA prompt variableIdentifies the customer
The one Who is the user? names (here user_id)No — kept exactlyNeverYes
Every other trait (name, plan, …)YesYes — {name}, {plan}No
  • How values are matched. User ID and custom fields: exactly, case-sensitive, up to 256 characters. Email: lower-cased; it must look like an address (up to 254 characters). Phone number: its digits, 8 to 15 of them, and the last ten count — so +91 98765 43210 and 098765 43210 are one person, and a caller with that number is the same person as the app user. Send the identifier as a string (an integer is read as its digits).
  • What is no identifier at all: empty, null, a boolean, an object, a decimal; a placeholder in any case — none, nil, null, undefined, nan, unknown, anonymous, anon, guest, test, 0, -, n/a, na; or an already-masked value such as [PHONE] or [EMAIL]. Such a conversation has no memory and cannot be the target of a call.
  • When it applies. Identity is fixed when a conversation starts; a sign-in during a conversation applies to the next one. You can call identify() before the SDK has loaded the agent's settings.
  • identify(null) signs out: the identity is forgotten on the device, the device is released from the customer and unlinked from their calls, and later conversations are anonymous. Identifying a different customer signs the previous one out first, and the chat on screen is cleared. With several agents, one identify() applies to all of them, and identify(null) signs out of all of them.
  • The memory choice (memory: false, or setMemory(false)) is kept for that customer on this install; nothing of theirs is recalled or stored (and, from 0.7.0, their conversation is not kept) until they turn it on again.

7.2Installs and the device limit

Each install gets an install ID the first time it runs — a random UUID, never shown to the agent, kept across launches: in the iOS keychain (this device only; it survives a reinstall), in Android app storage excluded from backups, through the native side in React Native (or the storage you give the client) and Flutter, and in the browser's localStorage on a website. Read it as installId.

Devices per user (1–5, default 2) caps how many installs can act as one customer. The first installs to identify as a customer are bound to them. Once the limit is reached, another install that claims the same identifier still works, but for that customer it gets no memory, cannot be rung for their calls, and is answered device_limit when it asks for or forgets their memory. A device is released by identify(null) on it, after 30 days unseen, or by Reset devices on the person's panel in Agent → Memory → People.

7.3Reading and erasing memory: memories(), setMemory(), forgetMemory()

PlatformWhat is rememberedForget itTurn it off / on
React Nativeclient.memories(): Promise<GraineMemory[]> · useGraineMemories()client.forgetMemory(): Promise<number>client.setMemory(enabled) · client.memoryEnabled
iOSmemories() async throws -> [GraineMemory]forgetMemory() async throws -> IntsetMemory(_:) · memoryChoice

WebsiteGraineAgent.memories(): Promise<Array>GraineAgent.forgetMemory(): Promise<number>GraineAgent.setMemory(enabled)

GraineMemory is { id, text, createdAt, updatedAt } (dates may be null), newest first, at most 100, already redacted. forgetMemory() returns how many were deleted and erases what is remembered for this agent's memory scope (for every agent sharing it when Shared with is Agents that share memory); with conversations that continue (0.7.0) it also clears the customer's kept conversation with this agent. Both work only for an identified customer on one of their devices (identity_required, device_limit otherwise).

iOS · Swift — a privacy screen
@MainActor final class PrivacyModel: ObservableObject {
    @Published var remembered: [GraineMemory] = []
    @Published var problem: String?

    func load() async {
        do { remembered = try await GraineInApp.shared.memories() }
        catch let error as GraineServiceError { problem = error.message }
        catch { problem = "Couldn't load what the assistant remembers." }
    }

    func forgetAll() async {
        do {
            let deleted = try await GraineInApp.shared.forgetMemory()
            remembered = []
            problem = "Deleted \(deleted) memories."
        } catch let error as GraineServiceError where error.code == .deviceLimit {
            problem = "Sign out on another device first."
        } catch { problem = "Couldn't delete them just now." }
    }

    func setRemembering(_ on: Bool) { GraineInApp.shared.setMemory(on) }
}
Android · Kotlin — a privacy screen
GraineInApp.get().memories { memories, error ->
    if (error != null) showProblem(error.message) else render(memories.orEmpty())   // main thread; exactly one is set
}
GraineInApp.get().forgetMemory { deleted, error ->
    if (error?.code == GraineErrorCode.DEVICE_LIMIT) showProblem("Sign out on another device first.")
    else if (error == null) showDone("Deleted $deleted memories.")
}
GraineInApp.get().setMemory(false)
React Native — a privacy screen
const client = useGraineClient();
const { memories, loading, error, refresh } = useGraineMemories();   // loads on mount and after forgetMemory
async function forgetAll() {
  try { const deleted = await client.forgetMemory(); show(`Deleted ${deleted} memories.`); }
  catch (e) { if (e instanceof GraineError) show(e.message); }
}
Flutter · Dart — a privacy screen
try {
  final remembered = await GraineInApp.instance.memories();
  final deleted = await GraineInApp.instance.forgetMemory();
} on GraineException catch (e) {
  if (e.code == GraineErrorCode.deviceLimit) showProblem('Sign out on another device first.');
}

7.4What Graine stores

Graine stores the identifier your app sends so your team can see who each conversation was with; the memory service only ever receives a one-way key derived from it.

  • The identifier is kept on each conversation's record with its field, in the form it is compared in (trimmed, an email lower-cased, a phone number as its last ten digits, at most 256 characters). Call History shows it as <field label> · <value> — User ID · u_8812, Email · asha@acme.example, Customer ID · C-20931 (a custom field's name written out) — and so do Agent → Memory → People and the person's panel. A call your team booked in the dashboard shows the identifier they typed from the moment it rings. It never becomes a prompt variable.
  • The user key — a one-way fingerprint of your workspace, the Who is the user? field and the value — is what memory, the kept conversation, devices and bookings are filed under. The same value in two workspaces gives two unrelated keys. Keys never change, so memory survives anything short of changing the identity setting. The install ID is kept only as a one-way key too.
  • Memory holds short facts, redacted before they are stored, for the agent's Keep memories for. Deleting an agent does not delete its memories early; they expire.
How far to trust an identifier

With a publishable key and no server of yours in the path, the identifier is what your app says. What bounds it: the device limit and the customer's own sign-out; rings that carry nothing personal; rate limits per key, per install and per address. Treat identity as recognising a returning customer, not as proof: before the agent discusses an account, confirm the customer through one of your actions.

8.Conversations continue

A customer who comes back — later today, tomorrow, on their other phone — sees the earlier messages in the chat window, and the agent picks up where they left off. Memory keeps long-term facts; this keeps the recent conversation itself.

8.1Who gets it

Exactly the customers memory applies to: an in-app or website conversation (a chat, the bar's voice, a native call) with an identified customer, on an agent whose memory is on, who has not opted out (memory: false), on a device that is one of theirs. Anyone else — anonymous, opted out, a device past the limit, a dashboard preview, a phone call — gets nothing kept and nothing restored. There is never a shared bucket.

8.2What is kept, and for how long

  • The most recent 50 messages per agent and customer — each { id, role, text, at, channel }, where channel is chat or voice — for 7 days after the last one (each new message renews the 7 days).
  • Per agent, even when memory is shared across agents: your support agent never shows your sales agent's chat. One customer's chat, bar calls and native calls with the same agent are one conversation.
  • Messages are kept as said — the same text Call History keeps — up to 2,000 characters each. Nothing is kept until the customer has said something in the conversation.

8.3What the customer sees, and what the agent knows

  • No repeated welcome. A new chat with earlier messages starts from them: the chat window receives the earlier conversation before any reply, and the scripted welcome message is not sent — the customer types next. The window opens on the conversation, not on the empty "New chat" state with its starters.
  • One row per voice call. Earlier chat messages are bubbles; a run of messages said on a call is one compact row, Voice call · {time} (the transcript stays in Call History). Date separators (Today, Yesterday, a date) mark where the local day changes.
  • The agent receives the newest 20 turns (up to 8,000 characters) and is told it is continuing an earlier conversation and should not introduce itself again unless asked. A voice call still opens with its spoken greeting — a call is a new call — but the agent knows the history.
  • Restored turns are delivered (not live), carry their original times, and are marked restored on the chat turn: restored?: true on React Native's chat turns, restored: Bool on iOS's GraineChatTurn, restored: Boolean on Android's, restored (a bool) on Flutter's. A reconnect within the same app run receives the same history again, so nothing is duplicated; the SDK's own messages still sending or failed stay after the restored ones.
React Native — drawing your own transcript
import { useGraineAgent, chatRows } from "@graineai/inapp-react-native";

function Transcript() {
  const { messages } = useGraineAgent();
  // chatRows groups the turns the way the built-in window does
  const rows = chatRows(messages, (turn) => ({ at: turn.at, voice: turn.channel === "voice" }));
  return rows.map((row) =>
    row.kind === "day" ? <DaySeparator key={row.key} label={row.label} />          // Today, Yesterday or a date
    : row.kind === "voice" ? <VoiceCallRow key={row.key} label={row.label} />      // one row per call: "Voice call · 6:05 PM"
    : <Bubble key={row.key} turn={row.item} faded={row.item.restored === true} />);
}
iOS · Swift — drawing your own transcript
// A bubble per chat turn; one row per run of voice turns (one call)
let turns = GraineInApp.shared.chat.turns
ForEach(Array(turns.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, turn in
    if turn.channel == .voice {
        if index == 0 || turns[index - 1].channel != .voice { VoiceCallRow(at: turn.at) }
    } else {
        Bubble(turn: turn, earlier: turn.restored)
    }
}

8.4Forgetting, opting out, and a new conversation

  • Forget clears it. Everything that deletes a customer's memory deletes the kept conversation too: forgetMemory() from your app (which, once it succeeds, also clears the chat on screen — a refusal leaves both as they were), Forget this person in the dashboard, and an agent tool that forgets.
  • Opting out (setMemory(false)) stops keeping and restoring it, but deletes nothing.
  • Sign-out (identify(null)) or another customer signing in clears the chat on screen.
  • New conversation. For a support-style chat that should start a fresh thread, the SDKs add newConversation(): it ends this agent's chat connection, asks Graine to drop the kept conversation for this agent and customer, clears the window, and opens a fresh chat — the scripted welcome and the starters appear again. Memory facts are untouched, and Call History keeps every earlier conversation. For an anonymous customer it clears the window only. The built-in chat window shows a New conversation control in its header (a compose icon beside close) while the window holds earlier, restored messages; it needs no confirmation. The agent's design can hide that control (Garage → Chat window → New conversation button); newConversation() still works from a button of yours.
  • Earlier messages on screen. The design can also hide them (Garage → Chat window → Earlier messages): the window then opens like a new chat, while the agent still receives the history and continues. The Garage previews it as the Returning customer moment.
PlatformStart a new conversation
React Nativeclient.newConversation(): Promise<void>
iOSGraineInApp.shared.chat.newConversation() async throws
AndroidGraineInApp.get().chat.newConversation(done: GraineCallback<Unit>? = null)
FlutterGraineInApp.instance.chat.newConversation() (on GraineChatSession)
WebsiteGraineAgent.newConversation()
Kotlin MPGraine.chat.newConversation() (a suspend function)

Older SDKs ignore the earlier conversation and show an empty chat as before; nothing breaks.

9.Chat, voice, components, screen context and actions

What a customer can use is the dashboard's What visitors get (Call and chat, Voice only, Chat only) and Opens on. An app can choose among those, never add one. One conversation runs at a time: opening the chat ends a voice call in the bar, and a native call ends both.

9.1Voice in the assistant bar

The bar places the call, asks for the microphone if it must, shows the connection in words (Weak connection, No connection, Reconnecting…), draws captions and components, and ends the call. Each SDK exposes the same state for an app that draws its own bar: connected, connecting, ready, muted, a one-word phase (idle, connecting, reconnecting, thinking, speaking, listening), the line quality, captions, and whether the microphone was refused.

PlatformStart, end, muteState
React NativeThe GraineVoiceLauncher render prop's api.start(), api.end(), api.setMuted(m), api.retry()The same api (connected, phase, captions, quality, micDenied, …)
iOSGraineInApp.shared.voice.start(), end(), setMuted(_:), retry()GraineVoice is an ObservableObject
AndroidGraineInApp.get().voice.start(), end(), setMuted(muted), retry()Properties on GraineVoice; GraineListener callbacks
FlutterGraineInApp.instance.voice.start(), end(), setMuted(…), retry()GraineVoice is a ChangeNotifier
Kotlin MPGraine.voice.start(), end(), setMuted(…)Graine.voice.state (a StateFlow)

By default a call ends two seconds after the app leaves the foreground (endOnBackground); a native call (section 10) is the way to keep talking with the screen off.

9.2The chat window

The bar opens the chat where the agent offers it. Typed messages sent while offline wait (Waiting for connection…) and go in order when the chat reconnects, after drops, with a backoff of 1, 2, 4, 8, 15 and then 30 seconds; a message that cannot be sent is marked failed. The typing indicator shows from a send until the agent's first words, a component, or 12 seconds. The chat window also lists the customer's upcoming calls with Cancel.

React Native · TypeScript
const { messages, send, typing, connected } = useGraineAgent();   // the provider's chat
send("Where is my order?");

// UIKit: present(GraineChatViewController(), animated: true)
// Drive it: let chat = GraineInApp.shared.chat; chat.open(); chat.send("Where is my order?"); chat.close()

// or place GraineChatView in your layout; it draws GraineInApp.get().chat
val chat = GraineInApp.get().chat

)));

Chat window size

The Garage's Window size sets how big the chat opens: Compact (the window above the bar), Large (on a phone, a sheet from the bottom about 92% of the screen tall with a grab handle; on a tablet or computer, a 420-wide panel up to 760 tall) or Full screen (the whole screen inside the safe areas; on a computer the large panel, and the whole page below 640 px wide). An app can override it: the open call's argument wins over the app's configuration, which wins over the design.

PlatformApp defaultFor one open

9.3Components

Build components in the dashboard's components editor, tick them under On screen, and name them in the prompt (on a flow agent, in the step that should show them). The SDKs draw them in your design: the bar draws them by default; place a component view elsewhere if you prefer — iOS and Android GraineWidgetView, Flutter GraineWidgetView (with showComponents: false on the bar), React Native GraineWidget. A tap answers the agent as the customer's next turn (a sentence for the agent and structured data for your webhooks), and a component can open a screen in your app through your navigation action. A multi-select reply reads "label: a and b" — the button's label, then the names, for example "Taken: Morning and Evening" (no label: the names alone) — and in a text chat it is also the customer's own bubble; React Native exports the rule as manySummary(titles, label = "Compare"). A component's live data, when it comes from your API, has 8 seconds; after that the authored content is shown.

9.4Screen context

Tell the agent what the customer can see whenever the screen or a field changes. Values are masked on the device; an unchanged screen is not sent again; the first change goes at once and later ones at most every 400 ms; the newest screen is sent again when the connection comes back and when the app returns to the foreground. Give every field a status (empty, filled, invalid, pending, locked): it is what turns "need a hand?" into naming the field that is wrong. Taps on labelled controls are reported by themselves (captureTaps, on by default on iOS, Android, Flutter and Kotlin MP).

React Native · TypeScript
useGraineScreen({
  screen: "checkout_address", title: "Delivery address",
  journey: { name: "Checkout", step: 2, of: 3, next: "Payment" },
  fields: [{ name: "postal_code", label: "Postal code", value: postalCode, status: "invalid", error: "We don't deliver there yet" }],
});
// With navigationRef on the provider, every route is reported by name automatically.

GraineInApp.shared.setScreen(GraineScreen(

    fields: [GraineField(name: "postal_code", label: "Postal code", value: postalCode, status: .invalid, error: "We don't deliver there yet")]
))
GraineInApp.shared.updateField(GraineField(name: "postal_code", value: postalCode, status: .filled))
GraineInApp.shared.track("coupon_applied", data: ["code_length": 8])
