Your own sensitive formats can be added to the masking once at start-up: React Native addMaskRule(pattern, token), iOS GraineMasking.addRule(pattern:token:), Android and Flutter Masking.addRule(…), website GraineAgent.addMaskRule(pattern, token). Built in: PAN, Aadhaar, card and account numbers, phone numbers, email addresses.

9.5Actions

Declare each action on the agent (Embed & Widgets → Actions) and implement a handler with the same name. The handler runs on the main thread (iOS, Android), gets the agent's arguments, and answers ok, refused or error with a message the agent uses to say what happened. Answer within about five seconds: the SDKs tell the agent an action did not finish after 5.5–6 seconds (the website loader after 5.5). A throw is answered as error, and a declared action this build does not implement as refused.

React Native · TypeScript
useGraineAction("set_language", ({ language }) => {
  setLanguage(String(language));
  return { status: "ok", message: `The app is now in ${language}.` };
});
iOS · Swift
let unregister = GraineInApp.shared.registerAction("set_language") { args in
    guard let language = args["language"] as? String else { return .refused("No language was given.") }
    settings.setLanguage(language)
    return .ok("The app is now in \(language).")
}
// A handler that takes time answers through the deferred form:
GraineInApp.shared.registerAction("upload_document", deferred: { args, done in
    upload(args) { ok in done(ok ? .ok("Uploaded.") : .error("The upload failed.")) }
})
Android · Kotlin
val unregister = GraineInApp.get().registerAction("set_language") { args ->
    val language = args.optString("language")
    if (language.isEmpty()) ActionResult.refused("No language was given.")
    else { settings.setLanguage(language); ActionResult.ok("The app is now in $language.") }
}
Flutter · Dart
final unregister = GraineInApp.instance.registerAction('set_language', (args) async {
  final language = args['language'];
  if (language is! String) return const ActionResult.refused('No language was given.');
  await settings.setLanguage(language);
  return ActionResult.ok('The app is now in $language.');
});
Kotlin Multiplatform · Kotlin
val unregister = Graine.registerAction("set_language") { args ->
    val language = args["language"] as? String ?: return@registerAction GraineActionResult.refused("No language was given.")
    settings.setLanguage(language)
    GraineActionResult.ok("The app is now in $language.")
}
Website · JavaScript
GraineAgent.defineAction("scroll_to_section", ({ section }) => {
  const el = document.getElementById(section);
  if (!el) return { status: "refused", message: "That section is not on this page." };
  el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth" });
  return { status: "ok", message: `Scrolled to ${section}.` };
});

checkActions() (iOS, Android, React Native) compares what the build registered with what the agent declares — usable, undeclared, unhandled — for a test or a debug screen. On the website, navigate with window.location, not window.open (popup blockers stop a window opened from the widget's callback).

10.WhatsApp-style calls

Two directions, one native call engine in your app: the customer calls the agent from a button, or Graine rings the customer at a booked time. Calls are voice only (components are not drawn during a call), one at a time, and they keep going with the screen locked, in another app, or on a Bluetooth headset.

10.1The customer calls the agent: startCall

startCall returns the call's ID — call_ and a lowercase UUID, carried by every outcome — or nothing while another call is live. It asks for the microphone if it is missing, ends a conversation in the bar, opens the call (CallKit on iPhone, the SDK's call screen on Android), and connects with who_called = "customer", call_reason = your reason (send an identifier such as order_help) and your call variables (masked; up to 12 variables in all with those two, about 1 KB).

React Native · calls package
const id = await GraineCalls.startCall({ reason: "order_help", variables: { order: "A-1043" } });   // null while another call is live
iOS · Swift
let id = GraineInApp.shared.calls.startCall(reason: "order_help", variables: ["order": "A-1043"])   // nil while another call is live
Android · Kotlin
// Main thread, from an activity in the foreground (the microphone service may only start from there)
val id = GraineInApp.get().calls.startCall(this, reason = "order_help", variables = mapOf("order" to "A-1043"))
Flutter · Dart
final id = await GraineCalls.instance.startCall(reason: 'order_help', variables: {'order': 'A-1043'});
Kotlin Multiplatform · Kotlin
val id: String? = Graine.calls.startCall(reason = "order_help", variables = mapOf("order" to "A-1043"))

On iOS present GraineCallView while calls.showsCallScreen is true (section 6.3); Android opens GraineCallActivity itself; React Native and Flutter show the SDK's screen with callScreen: "sdk" (the default) or let you draw your own with "app".

10.2Graine rings the customer: hosted ringing

  1. Upload your push credentials once — an APNs key for iOS and a Firebase service account for Android, made as Create your credentials shows — in Workspace settings → In-app calling (section 5.6), until each platform shows Verified.
  2. Hand the SDK its push tokens. The SDK registers the device with Graine — with the install, the time zone, the app version and, when the customer is signed in on one of their devices, the customer — on every new token, when its details change, and otherwise at most daily; with several agents, under each agent's key. Sign-out unlinks the device from the customer.
  3. Book a call (section 11). When it is due, Graine rings the customer's newest device.
iOS · Swift
// didFinishLaunching, every launch — iOS hands over a VoIP push only after this has run
GraineInApp.shared.calls.enableVoIPPushes()     // with hosted ringing on, the SDK registers the VoIP token itself
Android · KotlinAcmeMessagingService.kt
class AcmeMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService() {
    override fun onNewToken(token: String) = GraineCalls.onNewToken(this, token)   // registers this device with Graine

    override fun onMessageReceived(message: RemoteMessage) {
        if (GraineCalls.handlePush(this, message.data)) return                     // a call: it rings, even with the app closed
        // …your app's other messages
    }
}
XMLAndroidManifest.xml, inside <application>
<service android:name=".AcmeMessagingService" android:exported="false">
    <intent-filter><action android:name="com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT" /></intent-filter>
</service>
React Native · calls package
// index.js, before AppRegistry.registerComponent — rings even when the app was closed
messaging().setBackgroundMessageHandler(async (m) => { await GraineCalls.handlePush(m.data ?? {}); });

// at launch
GraineCalls.enableVoIPPushes(() => {});                                           // iOS: the token is registered by the SDK
messaging().getToken().then((token) => GraineCalls.registerPushToken({ token }));  // Android
messaging().onTokenRefresh((token) => GraineCalls.registerPushToken({ token }));
messaging().onMessage((m) => GraineCalls.handlePush(m.data ?? {}));               // Android, app open
Flutter · Dart
@pragma('vm:entry-point')
Future<void> onBackgroundPush(RemoteMessage message) async {
  await GraineCalls.instance.handlePush(message.data);           // rings, even when the app was closed
}

// in main(), after Firebase.initializeApp()
FirebaseMessaging.onBackgroundMessage(onBackgroundPush);
FirebaseMessaging.onMessage.listen((m) => GraineCalls.instance.handlePush(m.data));
GraineCalls.instance.enableVoIPPushes((_) {});                  // iOS
FirebaseMessaging.instance.getToken().then((t) { if (t != null) GraineCalls.instance.registerPushToken(t); });   // Android
FirebaseMessaging.instance.onTokenRefresh.listen(GraineCalls.instance.registerPushToken);
Kotlin Multiplatform
// iOS, every launch
Graine.calls.enableVoIPPushes()
// Android, in your FirebaseMessagingService
override fun onNewToken(token: String) = Graine.calls.onNewToken(token)
override fun onMessageReceived(message: RemoteMessage) { if (Graine.calls.handlePush(message.data)) return }

What a ring carries: an APNs VoIP push (apns-push-type: voip, topic <bundle ID>.voip, priority 10, expiration 0 — now or never) or a data-only FCM message at high priority that lives 30 seconds, with exactly type: "agent_call", call_id, caller_name (the agent's call name), hosted: "1" and agent_id (the booking agent's ID, so an app with several agents answers with the right one). No reason, no variables, nothing about the customer: a push can wait at Apple or Google until the phone is reachable, so it carries only what the ring shows. The agent learns why it is calling when the call connects. A push your own server sends (with call_id, reason, caller_name, variables) still rings exactly as before, side by side.

10.3Create your credentials, click by click

You make these once per app, in your own Apple and Google accounts. Graine never sees those logins: you upload only the key file and its details.

iOS: an APNs key

You need an Apple Developer Program membership (the Account Holder or an Admin) and your app's bundle ID.

  1. Create the key. Go to developer.apple.com/account → Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles → Keys → +.
  2. Name it (for example "Graine calls") and tick Apple Push Notifications service (APNs). If Apple asks you to configure the key, choose Sandbox & Production and Team Scoped (All Topics). A key limited to one topic must include your app's VoIP topic, your.bundle.id.voip.
  3. Continue → Register → Download. The .p8 file downloads once only, so keep it somewhere safe. Note the Key ID (10 characters) shown with the key.
  4. Find your Team ID: the top-right corner of your developer account, or Membership details (10 letters and digits).
  5. Let the app receive pushes. Under Identifiers, open your app's bundle ID and check that Push Notifications is enabled. In Xcode, the app target → Signing & Capabilities → add Push Notifications, and Background Modes with Voice over IP and Audio, AirPlay, and Picture in Picture ticked. React Native (Expo) and Flutter set these through their configuration (section 6).
  6. In Graine: Workspace settings → In-app calling → iOS → Set up: the Bundle ID, Team ID, Key ID, the Push key (.p8 file), and Environment Automatic (each device's own).

One APNs key serves every app in your team, for ordinary and VoIP pushes alike. Graine's calls need no .p12 certificate and no Firebase on iOS.

Android: a Firebase service account

You need a Firebase project that contains your Android app, and a Google account that owns or edits it.

  1. Add Firebase to the app (skip this if it already uses Firebase): console.firebase.google.com → Add project (or open yours) → Add app → Android → your app's package name → download google-services.json into the app module (app/), then add Firebase Cloud Messaging to the app as your platform's part of section 6 shows.
  2. Check that messaging is on: Project settings → Cloud Messaging → Firebase Cloud Messaging API (V1) shows Enabled. The old legacy API is not used.
  3. Create the key: Project settings → Service accounts → Firebase Admin SDK → Generate new private key → Generate key. A .json file downloads; treat it like a password. For the least access, create a dedicated account instead: Google Cloud console → IAM & Admin → Service accounts → Create service account → role Firebase Cloud Messaging API Admin → Keys → Add key → JSON.
  4. In Graine: Workspace settings → In-app calling → Android → Set up: the Package name and the Service-account key (.json file).
Keep the key files out of your app.

Never put the .p8 file or the service-account .json in your app or a repository, and never send them by email. They are for Graine only: upload them in the dashboard, where they are encrypted with your workspace's own key and never shown again.

10.4The call screen: six moments

The SDKs draw the call screen from the Garage's Call screen tab: background, avatar (logo, glyph or the call name's initial) in the chosen shape, the call name in the design's heading face, the status in your words, and the controls in your order. The last design is kept on the device, so a ring that wakes a closed app is drawn the same way.

MomentStatus lineButtonsNotes
Scheduled call ringing"Scheduled call" (your Scheduled call ringing words)Decline · AnswerA call Graine rang at a booked time. A ring pulses from the avatar. On a locked iPhone, the system's incoming-call screen; on Android, the full-screen ring
Other call ringing"Incoming call" (Other call ringing)Decline · AnswerA ring your own server sent
Connecting"Connecting…"Mute · Speaker · EndAnswered, or placed by the customer; the line is opening (it must open within 15 seconds)
On the callThe timer (m:ss), with " · Muted" while muted — or, with the timer off, "Listening", "Speaking", "Muted"Mute (Unmute) · Speaker · End, in your order; End round or pillCaptions show the line being said when on. The avatar moves while the agent speaks (not with reduced motion). The chat button is not drawn on a native call
Ended"Call ended" (your words); "Call failed" or "Declined" for those endingsDimmedShows for about a second, then the screen closes
Missed"Missed call"Close · Call backA ring nobody answered. iOS keeps it on the call screen for 30 seconds (missedCall, callBack(), dismissMissedCall()); Android leaves a notification with Call back and shows the missed screen when it is opened. Call back calls the same agent with the missed call's reason

Android's call screen shows over the lock screen and turns the screen on; closing it never ends the call (the ongoing notification brings it back). An Android app can name its own call screen (GraineCallsConfig(callActivity = …)); it then shows over the lock screen, forwards onRequestPermissionsResult to calls, and handles the intent actions GraineCalls.ACTION_SHOW, ACTION_ANSWER, ACTION_MISSED and ACTION_CALL_BACK.

10.5Outcomes, and their webhooks

OutcomeWhenBooked call's statusWebhook
ringingThe phone is ringing (reported to Graine for its rings; React Native, Flutter and Kotlin MP also hand it to your listener)ringing—
answeredThe customer picked up an incoming call; an ended or failed followsanswered, then completedThe conversation's own events
declinedThe customer declined it. Nothing rings for that customer for 6 hours, and that call never rings againdeclinedcall_declined
missedNobody answered within the ring timeout; another call was live (Android reports it as busy); or, on iOS, Do Not Disturb, a Focus or the block list stopped it. A booked call can ring once more after your re-ring delaymissedcall_missed
endedA call that connected is over: local (the customer hung up), remote (the agent did) or failed (the line broke; calls do not reconnect), with its durationcompletedThe conversation's own events
failedIt never connected: the microphone was refused (or not granted within 60 seconds), the line did not open within 15 seconds, or the agent could not be reachedfailed—
(never rang)Its time passed before it could ring (calling hours, credit, the agent switched off, a recent decline, the daily limit)expiredcall_expired
(never rang)No device seen in the last 30 days, or no working credentialsno_device—

Your app hears every outcome through the calls listener — React Native GraineCalls.onOutcome(fn), iOS GraineCallsListener.onCallOutcome(_:callId:), Android GraineCallListener.onCallOutcome(callId, outcome), Flutter GraineCalls.instance.outcomes, Kotlin MP Graine.calls.outcomes. React Native and Flutter keep the last 20 outcomes and rings and hand them to the first listener, so an app launched by a push still hears them. The webhook events call_declined, call_missed and call_expired are opt-in: tick them in Agent → Integrations & Tools → Custom Webhook → Send these events, under In-app calls. On Android, Flutter, React Native and Kotlin MP an outcome also carries hosted (Graine rang it) and, for a call that connected, durationSeconds.

10.6Locked screens, other apps, weak networks

What happensiPhoneAndroid
The phone is locked when a ring arrivesThe system incoming-call screen, with your call name, icon and ringtoneThe full-screen ring (with the full-screen permission; otherwise a heads-up call notification), Answer and Decline
The screen locks during a callThe call goes on (CallKit and the audio background mode)The call goes on (the microphone foreground service)
The customer opens another appThe call goes on; the system shows it is liveThe call goes on; the ongoing notification has Hang up
A phone call comes in during the agent's callCallKit handles it as for any call appThe agent's call is held while the phone has the audio, and ends if the phone call is answered
Airplane mode, or the network drops, mid-callThe call ends: outcome ended, reason failed. Calls do not reconnect; offer a call back
The phone is offline when a ring is sentThe push expires; the booking is marked missed when its ring time runs out
A battery saver stops background work—Some phones stop a call after the screen locks: ask the customer to allow your app in battery settings

10.7Both directions, end to end

The customer calls the agentGraine rings the customer at a booked time
1. Configure the calls at launch (startCall shows it per platform), and identify the customer. 1. Credentials uploaded and Verified (click by click).
2. A call button calls startCall with a reason. 2. The push wiring of hosted ringing in place, and the customer identified.
3. The call screen opens; the agent hears who_called = "customer" and the reason. 3. Booking on in Agent → Calls & scheduling; a call booked by the app, the agent or your team (section 11), or Ring now for a test.
4. The conversation; the customer or the agent ends it. 4. At the time, the phone rings — on the lock screen too (the six moments); the customer answers, and the agent hears who_called = "scheduled" and the booking's reason.
5. The outcome reaches your listener: ended, with who ended it and how long it lasted. 5. The outcome reaches your listener and Graine; a decline or a missed ring can send its webhook (outcomes).
6. In both directions the conversation is in Call History with its transcript — and, for a booked call, the booking it came from.

11.Scheduled calls

A scheduled call is a booking for a customer that Graine rings on their phone when it is due — booked by the agent, by your app or website, or by your team.

11.1The rules every booking follows

The SDK reads the agent's rules with its settings: schedulingRules (a property; no request). Before the settings load, and from an older server, it holds the defaults with booking off.

Field (GraineSchedulingRules)DefaultDashboard setting
usersCanBookfalseUsers, from your app
minLeadMinutes5With at least this much notice — the soonest
maxDaysAhead14Booked at most this far ahead — the furthest ahead
maxPendingPerUser3At most this many upcoming calls per user
ringTimeoutSeconds45Ring for
callNamenoneName on the incoming call
hostedRinging, platformsfalse, emptyWhether Graine rings this workspace's apps, and on which platforms (Workspace settings → In-app calling)
earliest(now)now plus minLeadMinutes — the first time a picker should offer
latest(now)now plus maxDaysAhead days — the last
  • The calling window. Every booking must fall inside the agent's Calling Window, read in the customer's time zone (the device's IANA zone, which every booking and device registration carries). A booking outside it is refused with outside_window and a sentence naming a time that would work.
  • Quiet hours apply to calls the agent or your team book (refused at booking if inside them), never to a time the customer picked themselves.
  • When it is due, Graine checks again: a call more than 10 minutes late is not rung (expired); a call outside the window or quiet hours moves to the next opening (within the days-ahead limit, else expired); no ring within 6 hours of a decline; at most Ring each user at most rings a day; then the customer's newest device seen in the last 30 days (among the devices bound to them), trying the next one on a dead push token. Credit and a switched-off agent hold a ring for up to 10 minutes.
  • Who it rings. A booking made for an identified customer rings their app, on the devices they are signed in on. A booking from an app with no identified customer rings that install only. A booking from a device that is not one of the customer's is refused (device_limit).

reason (up to 120 characters) reaches the agent as call_reason when the call connects and never travels in the ring. A GraineScheduledCall is { id, at, status, source, reason, isUpcoming, canCancel }: at is the platform's date type (UTC; null only if Graine's time could not be read), isUpcoming is true while scheduled or ringing, and canCancel while scheduled. Only a call whose canCancel is true can be cancelled.

11.3Checks made on the device first

scheduleCall refuses on the device, before any request, from schedulingRules: scheduling_off when usersCanBook is false; too_soon before earliest(now) (React Native and the website allow 30 seconds' grace); too_far after latest(now); Flutter also refuses a reason over 120 characters (invalid_request; the website trims it). Graine then checks the rest: outside_window, too_many_pending, identity_required, device_limit, invalid_request and rate_limited (10 bookings an hour from one install). The scheduling refusals come with a sentence written for the customer — show it as it is.

11.4Booking by the agent

With The agent, during a conversation on, the agent can book a call back when the customer asks ("call me tomorrow at six"). It works out the time in the customer's zone and tells them the confirmed time, or the reason it could not book, in plain words. In your app or on your website the booking is for the conversation's identified customer (else its install) and rings their app; on a phone call it is an ordinary call back to the caller's number. Mention in the prompt when to offer a call back.

11.5Booking by your team

Agent → Calls & scheduling → Schedule a call: App user (by the identifier your Who is the user? setting names) or Phone number, When, Time zone, and What it's about. Ring now rings a user straight away as a test. Both follow the same rules, quiet hours included, and show in the Scheduled calls list with their status.

A website cannot ring.

A browser cannot receive a WhatsApp-style call. A call booked on your website — by the agent or with scheduleCall — is for the identified customer and rings their app on their phone. A customer with no app device seen in the last 30 days is not rung: the booking ends no_device. So does a booking from a website visitor who is not identified: it is made for the browser's install, which has nothing to ring. Identify the visitor before offering a booking on the web.

11.6Example: a "book a consultation call" sheet with the native pickers

This is the pattern the demo apps use: the system's own date and time pickers, in 5-minute steps, bounded by earliest(now) and latest(now), and the SDK's message shown as it is when a booking is refused. The calling hours are not encoded in the picker; Graine answers outside_window with a time that would work.

iOS · SwiftBookConsultationSheet.swift
import SwiftUI
import GraineInApp

struct BookConsultationSheet: View {
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss
    @State private var when = Date()
    @State private var problem: String?
    @State private var sending = false

    var body: some View {
        let rules = GraineInApp.shared.schedulingRules
        let range = rules.earliest()...rules.latest()
        NavigationStack {
            Form {
                Section {
                    DatePicker("Date", selection: $when, in: range, displayedComponents: .date).datePickerStyle(.graphical)
                    DatePicker("Time", selection: $when, in: range, displayedComponents: .hourAndMinute).datePickerStyle(.wheel)
                } footer: {
                    Text("Between \(rules.minLeadMinutes) minutes and \(rules.maxDaysAhead) days from now, within our calling hours.")
                }
                if let problem { Text(problem).foregroundColor(.orange) }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Book a consultation call")
            .toolbar {
                ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) {
                    Button(sending ? "Booking…" : "Book") {
                        sending = true
                        Task {
                            do {
                                _ = try await GraineInApp.shared.scheduleCall(at: when, reason: "Consultation")
                                dismiss()
                            } catch let error as GraineServiceError {
                                problem = error.message          // written for the customer
                            } catch {
                                problem = "Couldn't book the call. Try again."
                            }
                            sending = false
                        }
                    }
                    .disabled(sending || !rules.usersCanBook)
                }
            }
            .onAppear {
                UIDatePicker.appearance().minuteInterval = 5
                when = rules.earliest().addingTimeInterval(15 * 60)
            }
        }
    }
}
Android · Kotlin — Jetpack Compose (Material 3)
@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)
@Composable
fun BookConsultationSheet(onDone: () -> Unit) {
    val rules = GraineInApp.get().schedulingRules
    val earliest = rules.earliest(Date()).time
    val latest = rules.latest(Date()).time
    var problem by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    val dateState = rememberDatePickerState(
        initialSelectedDateMillis = earliest,
        selectableDates = object : SelectableDates {
            override fun isSelectableDate(utcTimeMillis: Long) =
                utcTimeMillis >= earliest - 86_400_000 && utcTimeMillis <= latest
        },
    )
    val timeState = rememberTimePickerState()
    Column(Modifier.padding(16.dp)) {
        Text("Book a consultation call", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge)
        DatePicker(state = dateState)
        TimePicker(state = timeState)
        problem?.let { Text(it, color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error) }
        Button(enabled = rules.usersCanBook, onClick = {
            val at = combineInDeviceZone(dateState.selectedDateMillis ?: earliest, timeState.hour, timeState.minute / 5 * 5)
            GraineInApp.get().scheduleCall(at, "Consultation") { call, error ->
                if (error != null) problem = error.message else onDone()      // main thread; the message is for the customer
            }
        }) { Text("Book") }
    }
}
Flutter · Dart — Material pickers
Future<void> bookConsultation(BuildContext context) async {
  final rules = GraineInApp.instance.schedulingRules;
  final now = DateTime.now();
  final first = rules.earliest(now), last = rules.latest(now);
  final day = await showDatePicker(context: context, initialDate: first, firstDate: first, lastDate: last);
  if (day == null || !context.mounted) return;
  final time = await showTimePicker(context: context, initialTime: TimeOfDay.fromDateTime(first));
  if (time == null) return;
  final at = DateTime(day.year, day.month, day.day, time.hour, time.minute ~/ 5 * 5);
  try {
    await GraineInApp.instance.scheduleCall(at: at, reason: 'Consultation');
  } on GraineException catch (e) {
    showMessage(e.message);                                    // written for the customer
  }
}
React Native — @react-native-community/datetimepicker
const { rules, schedule } = useGraineScheduling();
const [when, setWhen] = useState(() => new Date(rules.earliest().getTime() + 15 * 60_000));
const book = async () => {
  try { await schedule(when, "Consultation"); close(); }
  catch (e) { setProblem(e instanceof GraineError ? e.message : "Couldn't book the call."); }
};
// iOS: <DateTimePicker value={when} mode="datetime" display="inline" minuteInterval={5}
//        minimumDate={rules.earliest()} maximumDate={rules.latest()} onChange={(_, d) => d && setWhen(d)} />
Website — the browser's own picker
const rules = GraineAgent.schedulingRules;
const input = document.querySelector("#when");            // <input type="datetime-local" step="300">
input.min = toLocalInputValue(rules.earliest(new Date()));
input.max = toLocalInputValue(rules.latest(new Date()));

} catch (e) {

}

combineInDeviceZone, showMessage, toLocalInputValue, setProblem and close stand for your app's own helpers. The demo apps' full sheets also offer quick-time chips and, with two agents, which agent should call.

11.7The chat window's upcoming calls

The chat window of the iOS, Android, Flutter and Kotlin Multiplatform SDKs lists the customer's upcoming calls with Cancel — the Booked calls card, which the design can hide or retitle (Garage → Chat window). React Native's chat and the website have no such card. The same list is yours to read: iOS chat.upcomingCalls, refreshUpcomingCalls(), cancelUpcomingCall(id:); Android chat.upcomingCalls, refreshUpcomingCalls(), cancelUpcomingCall(id); Flutter chat.upcomingCalls, refreshUpcoming(), cancelUpcoming(id); React Native useGraineScheduling().

12.Several agents in one app

One app can run several agents — each with its own publishable key — and choose one per screen: a voice-first assistant on Home, a support chat in Help, a sales agent on Plans. Each agent is a separate session: its own design, chat, kept conversation, voice bar, actions and bookings. They never mix.

12.1What is per agent, and what is shared

Per agent (never mixed)Shared by every agent in the app
  • Its session and its Garage design (colours, chat title, starters, call screen, Window size)
  • Its chat and its kept conversation (continuation is per agent, even when memory is shared)
  • Its voice bar, its actions (each agent is offered only its own), its components
  • Its scheduling and memory requests, which go to that agent's key; its call screen design and call name
  • Who the customer is: identify() on any agent identifies them for all; identify(null) signs out everywhere (each agent reads its own Who is the user? field)
  • The install ID and the customer's memory choice
  • The current screen (each agent receives it while it has a live conversation)
  • The call engine, and the rule of one conversation at a time across all agents: starting a call or chat on one ends a live one on another

Memory facts are shared between agents only when both agents' Shared with is Agents that share memory; otherwise each agent remembers on its own.

12.2Worked example: a voice assistant and a separate support chat

The default agent is a voice-first assistant shown in the bar on every screen. A second agent named support is a support-style chat, opened full screen from your Help screen. In the dashboard they are two agents, each with its own key and its own Garage design:

Dashboard settingDefault agent (the assistant)support agent

Garage → Chat window (Make it yours → Chat)—Window size Full screen; its own Title ("Support"); its own Starters ("Track my order", "Talk to a person")

12.3Calls with several agents

  • Placing: startCall(…, agent: name) places the call with that agent (the default when omitted; an unknown name places nothing and logs an error, or rejects in React Native).
  • Rings are routed by agent. Graine's ring carries agent_id; the SDK answers it with the configured agent whose agent (or web-call variant) it names — that agent's call name, ring time, design and outcome reporting. A ring naming none of your agents rings with the default agent (and says so in the log).
  • Devices register once per agent key, so every agent's workspace can ring the phone. A missed call is called back on the agent that rang.

PlatformConfigureLook upViews take the agent

A name is trimmed; an empty name is the default agent; configuring a name again returns that agent unchanged. The default agent is the one configured without a name, else the first one configured.

13.SDK reference

Every public declaration of each SDK, read from its source for 0.7.0 (React Native 0.41.0, calls 0.2.0, loader 1.2.0): the signature, what it returns, the errors it can raise, and what it does. The data structures, across the platforms and with what to expect from each, come first. Within a platform, the agent's entry point comes first, then chat, voice, views, calls, scheduling, memory, errors, screen context and actions, and finally the lower-level types the SDK's own components are built from (public, but not needed for an integration).

How errors arrive

React Native and the website: promises reject with GraineError (code, message, status, retryAfterSeconds). iOS: async throws a GraineServiceError (code: GraineErrorCode, message, retryAfterSeconds, status). Android: the callback's error, a GraineError (code, message, retryAfterSeconds), on the main thread — never thrown. Flutter: GraineException (message, code, codeName, statusCode, retryAfterSeconds). Kotlin MP: GraineException (code, message, retryAfterSeconds). Calling before start-up is a programming error: iOS stops with a message, Android throws IllegalStateException, Flutter throws StateError.

13.1Data structures, and what to expect

Every type the SDKs hand your app, across the platforms: its exact name on each, every field with its type and default, and what to expect — when it appears or changes, what can be empty, times and time zones, and the edge cases. The per-platform tables after this part list every member of every type. Types are written Swift (iOS) · Android (Kotlin) · KMP (Kotlin Multiplatform) · Dart (Flutter) · TS (TypeScript: React Native, and the website where it applies).

Three rules that hold everywhere
  • Names. A type has the same name on every platform. Enum cases follow each language: Swift .noDevice, Android NO_DEVICE, KMP NoDevice, Dart noDevice, TS "noDevice" — the word Graine sends is no_device. The status, source and error-code types keep that word in wire (Swift, Kotlin, Dart).
  • Times are moments, not wall-clock readings. Swift Date, Android java.util.Date, KMP Instant, Dart DateTime in UTC (call .toLocal() to show it), TS Date for bookings and memories, and a number of milliseconds since the epoch for chat turns and call timers. Show them in the device's time zone. A booking you send carries the device's offset (for example 2026-10-14T18:00:00+05:30) and its time zone, and Graine applies the agent's calling hours in the customer's own time zone.
  • Values from a newer Graine never crash an older SDK. A status, source or error code the SDK does not know arrives as Swift .unknown(String), Kotlin Unknown(raw) (its wire holds the word), Dart unknown (the word in statusName, sourceName or codeName) and TS the word itself (the unions end in string & {}). Give every switch a default case.

GraineChatTurn — one message in the chat

iOS GraineChatTurn in GraineInApp.shared.chat.turns · Android GraineChatTurn in chat.messages · Flutter GraineChatTurn in GraineInApp.instance.chat.turns · React Native Turn in useGraineAgent().messages (the client's own chat state uses ChatTurn, with the same fields) · KMP GraineChatTurn in Graine.chat.turns (a StateFlow), with Android's fields. The website's widget draws the chat itself and hands no turns to the page. Oldest first, always.

FieldTypeMeaning, and what to expect
idSwift, Kotlin, Dart String · TS id?: stringSwift, Kotlin, Dart: t1, t2, …, stable for the life of the transcript. React Native: ties a waiting message to its sending. A restored turn keeps Graine's id.
roleSwift GraineRole (.agent, .customer) · Android Role (AGENT, CUSTOMER) · KMP GraineRole (USER, AGENT) · Dart GraineChatRole (user, agent) · TS "agent" | "customer"Who said it.
textString · TS stringThe words. Grows while live. Can be empty for an agent turn that only drew a component.
atSwift Date · Android java.util.Date · KMP Instant · Dart DateTime (UTC) · TS at?: number (ms since the epoch)When the turn began (an agent's: its first words). A restored turn keeps the time it was said.
liveBool · TS live?: booleanThe agent's words are still arriving: draw them as provisional. The same turn (same id) updates until live is false. Restored turns are never live.
deliverySwift GraineChatTurn.Delivery (.sending, .sent, .failed) · Android GraineChatTurn.Delivery (SENDING, SENT, FAILED; default SENT) · KMP GraineDelivery? · Dart GraineChatDelivery? · TS pending?: booleanA customer's message only (an agent's turn is sent, or null in KMP and Dart). sending: typed while the chat was not connected; it goes as soon as it is. failed: every reconnect was spent — the next message, or the chat's retry, sends it again. React Native marks only pending.
proactiveBool · TS proactive?: booleanThe agent spoke without being asked: its welcome, or something it noticed.
componentAndroid GraineComponent? · Dart GraineComponent? · KMP GraineComponent? (on Android)What the agent drew with this turn. iOS draws components in its component views and React Native in widgets, so neither puts them on the turn.
restoredSwift Bool · Android, KMP Boolean (default false) · Dart bool (default false) · TS restored?: trueFrom an earlier conversation, restored when the chat opened: delivered, with its own time and id, not said just now.
channelSwift GraineChatChannel (.chat, .voice) · Android GraineChatTurn.Channel (CHAT, VOICE) · KMP GraineChatChannel (CHAT, VOICE) · Dart GraineChatChannel (chat, voice) · TS channel?: "voice" (absent for the chat)Where it was said. Only a restored turn can be voice.
  • Restored turns arrive once, when the chat opens, before any reply — only for an identified customer, on an agent with memory on, who has not opted out, on one of their devices. At most 50, oldest first, delivered and never live; the welcome message is not sent then. A reconnect in the same app run receives them again and the SDK does not duplicate them.
  • A run of consecutive voice turns is one row, "Voice call · {time}" — the built-in window never shows what was said on a call (Call History keeps it). React Native's chatRows and Kotlin Multiplatform's GraineChatRows group them for a transcript of your own.
  • The list empties on sign-out (identify(null)), when another customer signs in, after a successful forgetMemory(), and on newConversation().

Chat state — is the chat connected?

PlatformWhereWhat you get
iOSGraineInApp.shared.chat.status (published)GraineChatStatus: .idle (not in the chat: never opened, left, or the app is in the background) · .connecting · .online · .reconnecting(attempt:) (an attempt out of six) · .offline (it could not reconnect, or the conversation was ended; a message or retry() connects again). Beside it: online, status.isConnecting, typing, isOpen, upcomingCalls.
AndroidGraineInApp.get().chatconnected, connecting, failed (every retry spent), online, typing, messages, upcomingCalls (soonest first, at most three).
FlutterGraineInApp.instance.chat (a ChangeNotifier)connected, connecting, agentTyping, failed, error (why the last connect failed, for a log; null once connected), isOpen, turns, upcomingCalls.
React NativeuseGraineAgent(); the clientconnected, connecting, reconnecting, typing, surface ("call" or "chat": which one the customer is in). The client's conversation is "call", "chat" or null when nothing is live.
Kotlin MPGraine.chat.status (StateFlow<GraineChatStatus>)IDLE · CONNECTING · ONLINE · RECONNECTING · OFFLINE; beside it typing and turns.
Website—The widget shows its own state ("Online", reconnecting). The page opens and closes it; no chat events reach the page.

Reconnecting. When the connection drops, the native SDKs try six times — 1, 2, 4, 8, 15 and 15 seconds apart — and then go offline until the customer sends something or the app retries. React Native waits 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 seconds, then keeps trying every 30 seconds for as long as the chat is open. One conversation at a time on a device: opening the chat ends a call the bar holds, and a native call holds the chat until it is over.

GraineChatSize — how big the chat window opens

iOS GraineChatSize (.compact, .large, .full) · Android GraineChatSize (COMPACT, LARGE, FULL) · Flutter GraineChatSize (compact, large, full) · React Native ChatSize ("compact" | "large" | "full") · KMP GraineChatSize (COMPACT, LARGE, FULL) · the website takes the same three words as plain strings.

  • Which size wins: the size passed to the open call (chat.open(size:), chat.open(size), GraineChat.open(context, size:), openChat({ size }), Graine.chat.open(size), GraineAgent.open({ size })), then the app's chatSize, then the agent's design (Window size in the Garage), else compact.
  • An open's own size lasts until the chat closes; moving to the call and back keeps it.
  • On a phone, large is a sheet over about 92% of the screen and full the whole screen inside the safe areas; on a tablet or computer, large and full open a panel 420 wide and up to 760 tall; on a web page narrower than 640 px, large is a sheet and full the whole page.
  • A size word the SDK does not know (from a newer design) is passed over: the next rule decides.

newConversation() — a fresh thread

PlatformCallFails with
iOSGraineInApp.shared.chat.newConversation() async throws; Objective-C newConversationWithCompletion:GraineServiceError (deviceLimit, network, …)
AndroidGraineInApp.get().chat.newConversation(done: GraineCallback<Unit>? = null)the callback's GraineError
FlutterFuture<void> newConversation() on GraineInApp.instance.chatGraineException
React Nativeclient.newConversation(): Promise<void>, also on useGraineAgent()rejects with GraineError
WebsiteGraineAgent.newConversation() → Promiserejects with a code
Kotlin MPsuspend fun newConversation() on Graine.chatGraineException
  • It returns nothing. On success the chat hangs up, Graine drops the conversation it kept for this agent and customer, the window clears and — when the customer was in the chat — a fresh chat opens with the welcome and the starters.
  • Memory facts are untouched, and Call History keeps the earlier conversation. With nobody identified nothing was kept, so only the screen clears.
  • A refusal (for example device_limit) leaves the chat as it was, connected again. A call in progress is left alone.
  • The window's own New conversation control does the same. The agent's design can hide that control; the call still works from a button of yours.

identify() — who the customer is

PlatformCall
iOSGraineInApp.shared.identify(_ traits: [String: Any?]?, memory: Bool? = nil)
AndroidGraineInApp.get().identify(traits: Map<String, Any?>?, memory: Boolean? = null)
FlutterGraineInApp.instance.identify(Map<String, Object?>? traits, {bool? memory})
React Nativeclient.identify(user: Record<string, unknown> | null, { memory?: boolean }); useGraineIdentify()
WebsiteGraineAgent.identify(traits, { memory })
Kotlin MPGraine.identify(traits: Map<String, Any?>?, memory: Boolean? = null)
  • What is sent. The value of the trait the agent's Who is the user? field names (user_id unless the dashboard chose email, phone or a custom field) goes as it is, only with the requests that start a conversation — never into prompt variables or the screen context. Every other trait becomes a prompt variable, masked on the device.
  • What is kept. The identifier is stored with the conversation, so your team can find the person in the dashboard; memory is filed under a one-way key made from it, not the value.
  • A placeholder ("guest", "null", a masked [EMAIL]), null, a boolean or a fraction identifies nobody: that conversation is anonymous, with no memory.
  • memory: false — this customer's conversations are neither remembered nor recalled, kept on the device for them; left out — their last choice stands (on until they make one).
  • Identity is fixed per conversation: a change reaches the next one. One customer for the whole app: every configured agent hears it.
  • identify(null) signs out: the device stops being that customer's and a chat open for them ends with its transcript. Someone else signing in without a sign-out first signs the last customer out the same way.

GraineMemory — one thing the agent remembers

FieldTypeMeaning, and what to expect
idStringThe memory's id.

createdAtSwift Date? · Android java.util.Date? · KMP Instant? · Dart DateTime? (UTC) · TS Date | nullWhen it was first remembered; null when Graine did not say.

  • memories() returns a list — Swift [GraineMemory], Android List<GraineMemory> in the callback, Dart List<GraineMemory>, TS GraineMemory[] (React Native also has useGraineMemories()), the website plain { id, text, createdAt, updatedAt } objects, KMP List<GraineMemory> — newest first, at most 100. Only for the identified customer on one of their devices; otherwise identity_required or device_limit.
  • forgetMemory() returns how many memories were deleted — Swift Int, Android Int in the callback, Dart int, TS number, KMP Int — and deletes the kept conversation as well. When it succeeds the chat on screen clears; a failure, unavailable included, leaves both as they were.

Session settings the app can read

The agent's settings load once per launch. Until then the session is empty and the booking rules are the defaults, with booking off — on iOS and Android, the last rules kept on the device. A setting an older server does not send means its default: user_id, 2 devices per user.

GraineScheduledCall — a booked call

Returned by scheduleCall and, as a list, by scheduledCalls(), on every platform under this name (the website returns plain objects of the same shape). Upcoming first.

FieldTypeMeaning, and what to expect

Return types: scheduleCall → GraineScheduledCall (status scheduled); scheduledCalls() → a list of them; cancelScheduledCall(id) → the GraineCallStatus afterwards, cancelled when Graine does not say (the website resolves the word, "cancelled"). Signatures per platform: section 11.2.

GraineCallStatus — where a booked call is

StatusWhat it means
scheduledBooked, waiting for its time. The only status that can be cancelled.
ringingGraine is ringing the customer's device now.
answeredThe customer answered; the conversation is on.
completedThe call took place and ended.
declinedThe customer declined the ring. Nothing rings them again for 6 hours.
missedIt rang out with no answer.
failedIt could not be rung or connected.
cancelledCalled off before it rang.
expiredIts time passed while it could not ring: more than 10 minutes late, or no opening left in the calling hours within the days-ahead limit.
no_deviceGraine had no device of this customer's to ring: none of theirs seen in the last 30 days (a website visitor's browser cannot ring).
unknown(raw)A status newer than this SDK, carrying its word.

Names: Swift .scheduled … .noDevice, .unknown(String) · Android GraineCallStatus.SCHEDULED … NO_DEVICE, Unknown(raw) · KMP GraineCallStatus.Scheduled … NoDevice, Unknown · Dart scheduled … noDevice, unknown · TS "scheduled" … "noDevice", or the new word. Read it from Graine with Swift GraineCallStatus(wire:), Kotlin GraineCallStatus.from(wire), Dart GraineCallStatus.fromWire.

GraineCallSource — who booked it

agent (the agent, in a conversation) · app (your app, through the SDK; the word Graine sends is sdk) · dashboard (your team) · api · unknown(raw). Swift .agent …, Android AGENT, APP, DASHBOARD, API, KMP Agent, App, Dashboard, Api, Dart agent, app, dashboard, api, TS "agent" | "app" | "dashboard" | "api".

GraineSchedulingRules — what may be booked

iOS GraineInApp.shared.schedulingRules · Android GraineInApp.get().schedulingRules · Flutter GraineInApp.instance.schedulingRules · React Native client.schedulingRules (and useGraineScheduling().rules) · website GraineAgent.schedulingRules · KMP Graine.schedulingRules. A property — no request.

FieldType, defaultMeaning, and what to expect
usersCanBookBool, falseCustomers may book from the app (Users, from your app). False when the settings say nothing.
minLeadMinutesInt, 5The least notice a booking may give.
maxDaysAheadInt, 14How far ahead a booking may be.
maxPendingPerUserInt, 3The most calls one customer may have waiting.
ringTimeoutSecondsInt, 45How long a ring Graine sends lasts before it is missed: 20–60 seconds, as the dashboard allows; every SDK holds a value outside that range to it.
callNameString?, nullThe name the phone shows when Graine rings; null — the agent's name.
hostedRingingBool, falseGraine rings this workspace's apps (push credentials uploaded).
platformslist, emptyWhere Graine rings: ios, android (Swift [GraineRingPlatform], KMP List<GrainePlatform>, the others strings). Android adds ringsAndroid.
earliest(now)→ a timenow plus minLeadMinutes: the first time a picker should offer.
latest(now)→ a timenow plus maxDaysAhead days: the last.

Checked on the device first. scheduleCall refuses before sending anything when booking is off (scheduling_off), the time is before earliest(now) or not in the future (too_soon; the website allows 30 seconds' grace), or after latest(now) (too_far) — these errors have status 0. Graine checks again, and checks what only it knows: the calling hours, the calls already waiting.

GraineCallOutcome — what became of a call

Reported once per call — iOS GraineCallsListener.onCallOutcome(_:callId:), Android GraineCallListener.onCallOutcome(callId, outcome), Flutter GraineCalls.instance.outcomes (a stream), React Native GraineCalls.onOutcome(fn), KMP Graine.calls.outcomes (a flow that does not replay: collect it from app start). Send it to your server with the call id. For a call Graine rang (hosted), the SDK has already told Graine.

FieldTypeMeaning, and what to expect
callIdString (iOS: the listener's argument)Your server's call_id, Graine's for a hosted ring, or the id startCall returned.
outcomeSwift GraineCallOutcome (.answered, .declined, .missed, .ended(GraineCallEndReason), .failed(String)) · Android kind: GraineCallOutcome.Kind (ANSWERED, DECLINED, MISSED, ENDED, FAILED) · KMP outcome: GraineCallOutcome.Kind · Dart outcome: GraineCallOutcomeKind · TS outcome stringanswered, declined, missed, ended, failed; React Native, Flutter and KMP also report ringing when a ring starts. One word for your server: wire.
reasonDart, KMP reason: String? · TS reason (with ended) or error (with failed) · Swift endReason, error · Android endReason, error, reasonWith ended: local (this app hung up), remote (the agent did) or failed (the line broke). With failed: why it never connected, for your logs.
durationSecondsInt? · TS number | nullWith ended: how long the conversation lasted, in whole seconds. Android, Flutter, React Native, KMP.
hostedBool, falseGraine rang it (a booked call), rather than your server's push. Android, Flutter, React Native, KMP.
busyBoolean, false (Android)A missed ring refused because another call was live.
agentString? (Dart, TS, KMP)The configured agent the call was with — "default", or the name it was configured under. Null when the platform cannot say (on Android, a ring refused while another call was live).

Do not rely on the order of an outcome relative to the call's state changes.

When each happens, which methods raise it and what to do (retry, wait retryAfterSeconds, or fix the set-up): section 14.1. Branch on the code; the message is a sentence fit to show the customer and never carries the identifier, traits or a push token.

Several agents

iOS GraineInApp.configure(_:name:), GraineInApp.named(_:), GraineInApp.all, GraineInApp.shared · Android GraineInApp.init(application, config, name), GraineInApp.get(name), GraineInApp.find(name), GraineInApp.all, GraineInApp.DEFAULT · Flutter GraineInApp.init(config, name:), GraineInApp.named(name), GraineInApp.all, GraineInApp.instance · React Native one GraineProvider per agent; calls GraineCalls.configure({ agents }), DEFAULT_AGENT · KMP Graine.configure(config, name), Graine.agent(name), Graine.agents · website one agent on the page at a time, switched with GraineAgent.load(). The default agent's name is "default" everywhere. What is per agent and what is shared: section 12.1.

What the SDKs handle for you (for the curious)

  • The history frame — the one frame a continued chat opens with, before any reply: { "type": "history", "turns": [{ "id", "role", "text", "at", "channel" }], "continued": true }. Roles are user / assistant, at is ISO-8601 UTC, channel is chat or voice, at most 50 turns, each text at most 2,000 characters. The SDKs turn it into restored GraineChatTurns; a turn they cannot read is skipped.
  • The website's messages to its widget — graine:identity { value, installId, memory, timezone } (who the visitor is, the browser's install ID, the memory choice and the IANA time zone), graine:window { size, layout }, graine:new-conversation and graine:memory-forgotten. They travel only between your page and Graine's frame.

13.2React Native — @graineai/inapp-react-native 0.41.0

TypeScript. Everything below is exported from @graineai/inapp-react-native (subpaths /mask and /client re-export the same names). Hooks need a GraineProvider above them, unless setDefaultClient(client) was called. Requests to Graine reject with GraineError.

GraineError

class GraineError extends Error — What a request to Graine rejects with: a code (branch on it), a message for the customer, the HTTP status (0 when nothing answered) and how long to wait for rate_limited.

readonly retryAfterSeconds: number | nullnumber | null—With rate_limited: how long the route asked to be left alone, when it said.

13.4iOS — GraineInApp 0.7.0

GraineInApp

The SDK's entry point: one instance per configured agent, made by GraineInApp.configure(_:name:) at launch and reached as GraineInApp.shared (the default agent) or GraineInApp.named(_:). Its methods may be called from any thread; voice, calls and chat are main-thread objects, and listeners are called on the main thread.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
@discardableResult static func configure(_ config: GraineConfig, name: String = "default") -> GraineInApp GraineInApp — Configures an agent. Call it once, at launch (App.init or application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:)). Without a name it is the default agent — the one shared returns and every view draws unless handed another; an app with several agents configures each under its own name and publishable key. The name is trimmed, and an empty name is the default. A second call with a name already configured returns that agent unchanged. A new agent takes on who is signed in, the memory choice and the current screen, and starts loading its settings from Graine.
static func named(_ name: String) -> GraineInApp? GraineInApp? — The agent configured under name (trimmed), or nil.
static var all: [String: GraineInApp] { get } [String: GraineInApp] — Every configured agent, keyed by name.
static var current: GraineInApp? { get } GraineInApp? — The default agent — or, when every agent was given a name, the first one configured. Nil before any agent is configured.
static var shared: GraineInApp { get } GraineInApp — The same agent as current. Stops the app with a message if no agent has been configured: call configure first.
typealias ActionHandler = ([String: Any]) throws -> GraineActionResult — — The handler type for registerAction(_:handler:): it receives the agent's arguments and returns the answer, and may throw.
typealias DeferredActionHandler = ([String: Any], @escaping (GraineActionResult) -> Void) -> Void — — The handler type for registerAction(_:deferred:): it receives the arguments and a done callback to answer with later.
let config: GraineConfig GraineConfig — The configuration this agent was made with.
let name: String String — The name this agent was configured under; "default" for the default agent.
var session: GraineSessionConfig? { get } GraineSessionConfig? — The agent's settings from the dashboard, once loaded (once per launch); nil before. onSessionReady reports it.
var design: GraineDesign? { get } GraineDesign? — The brand's design from the session: light and dark tokens and which to use. Nil before the session loads, and from a server that sends none; the SDK's views then draw from the dashboard's appearance settings.
var theme: GraineThemeTokens? { get } GraineThemeTokens? — The design tokens to draw right now: the brand's fixed scheme, else the device's current light or dark, picked again whenever the device switches. Nil without a design. onTheme reports each change.
private(set) lazy var voice: GraineVoice GraineVoice — The in-app voice call that GraineAgentBar uses. Attach it to your window before starting a call. Main thread only.
var calls: GraineCalls { get } GraineCalls — Native calls on CallKit and VoIP pushes: the customer calling your agent, or your agent ringing the customer. One object for the whole app — every agent's calls is the same object, and startCall(reason:variables:agent:) picks the agent. Main thread only.
private(set) lazy var chat: GraineChat GraineChat — The typed conversation with this agent. GraineChatView and the bar use it themselves. Main thread.
func addListener(_ listener: GraineListener) nothing — Hear everything this agent reports. Held weakly — keep your own reference. Adding the same listener twice has no effect. Callbacks arrive on the main thread.
func removeListener(_ listener: GraineListener) nothing — Stops reporting to that listener.
func identify(_ traits: [String: Any?]?, memory: Bool? = nil) nothing — Who is signed in, for every configured agent. The trait the agent's Identity setting names (user_id unless the dashboard says email, phone or a custom trait) identifies the customer for memory and for the calls Graine rings: its value travels only with the requests that start a conversation, never as a prompt variable. Every other trait becomes a prompt variable, masked on the device; nested objects and arrays are dropped. A placeholder value ("guest", "null", a masked "[EMAIL]") is no identity, and those conversations are anonymous. memory: false means this customer's conversations are neither remembered nor recalled; nil keeps their last choice (true until they make one). The identity is fixed per conversation: a change applies to the next one. identify(nil) signs out: the device stops being that customer's, Graine is told, and later conversations are anonymous. When a different customer signs in, or the customer signs out, the chat transcript on screen is cleared.
func setMemory(_ enabled: Bool) nothing — Whether the current customer's conversations are remembered, for every agent — the same as calling identify again with memory: enabled. Kept on the device for that customer; applies to the next conversation.
var memoryChoice: Bool { get } Bool — The current customer's memory choice: true until they turn it off. When false, nothing is recalled or stored.
var installId: String { get } String — This install's id: a UUID made on first launch and kept in the Keychain (this device only), surviving reinstalls. The same for every agent. Graine counts a customer's devices by it; the agent never sees it. If the Keychain cannot keep it, that launch uses a new one.
@discardableResult func forgetMemory() async throws -> Int Int GraineServiceError: identity_required, device_limit, rate_limited, network, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refused Deletes everything this agent's memory holds about the signed-in customer. Waits for the session first. Throws identity_required before sending anything when nobody is identified, and device_limit from a device that is not one of the customer's. Returns how many memories were deleted (0 when Graine does not say). The kept conversation goes too, and the chat on screen clears — only when it succeeds; a refusal leaves both as they were.
func memories() async throws -> [GraineMemory] [GraineMemory] GraineServiceError: identity_required, device_limit, rate_limited, network, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refused What the agent remembers about the signed-in customer, newest first, at most 100, already redacted — to show people what is kept about them. Waits for the session first, and throws identity_required before sending anything when nobody is identified.
func setVariables(_ values: [String: Any?]?) nothing — Prompt variables from the app's own data, while it runs. Merged, not replaced: nil under a key removes it, nil for the whole map clears them. Values become strings (nested objects and arrays are dropped) and are masked. They reach the next call; an engine page already loaded is updated too.
func currentVariables() -> [String: String] [String: String] — Every variable the agent will receive, merged in precedence order: the dashboard's defaults, then GraineConfig.variables, then setVariables, then the traits from identify (without the identifying trait).
func setScreen(_ next: GraineScreen?) nothing — What the customer is looking at; call it on every meaningful change. Shared by every agent. An unchanged screen is not resent, and bursts are coalesced to one frame per 400 ms — the first goes at once. nil means no screen.
func updateField(_ field: GraineField) nothing — Reports one changed field, merged by name into the current screen (added when new), so a form need not describe itself again on every keystroke. Does nothing without a current screen, or for a field with an empty name.
func removeField(_ name: String) nothing — Removes a field from the current screen. Nothing happens if it was never reported.
func clearScreen(_ screenId: String?) nothing — Forgets the screen only if it is still the one with that id — safe in a screen's teardown, which can run after the next screen has reported itself. nil clears whatever screen is set.
func track(_ name: String, data: [String: Any] = [:]) nothing — A product event that informs the agent without interrupting. It rides the next context frame; the last 10 are kept. Every agent hears it. An empty name is ignored.
func tap(_ name: String, data: [String: Any] = [:]) nothing — Records a tap on a named control as tap:<name> (the name trimmed, inner spaces collapsed, cut to 60 characters; an empty name is ignored). Taps are context, not news: they ride the next frame, at the end of its 400 ms window. Every agent hears it.
func noteInteraction() nothing — The customer did something that is not a field edit — scrolled a list, opened a picker, sent a message — so the idle clock that detects a stuck customer restarts. Field edits do not count.
func configureFriction(_ override: GraineFrictionConfig?) nothing — Replaces the app's layer of friction rules, applied over the dashboard's; nil removes it. Safe at any time.
@discardableResult func reopenComponent() -> Bool Bool — Puts back the last component the customer closed without answering, exactly as it was — for a "show that again" control. Returns false when there is none.
@discardableResult func registerAction(_ name: String, handler: @escaping ActionHandler) -> () -> Void () -> Void — unregisters — Something the agent can do in your app; declare it on the agent in the dashboard too — a handler with no declaration is never offered, and a declaration with no handler is refused. The handler runs on the main thread and must answer within six seconds, or the agent is told it was not done; a handler that throws answers error with the error's description. Registering the same name again replaces the handler. The returned function unregisters it, if it is still this registration.
@discardableResult func registerAction(_ name: String, deferred handler: @escaping DeferredActionHandler) -> () -> Void () -> Void — unregisters — The same, for work that finishes later — an upload, a network call. Call done exactly once, from any thread; later calls are ignored. After six seconds the agent is told the app did not answer, so slower work should answer at once and report its outcome later with setScreen or track.
func checkActions() -> GraineActionCheck GraineActionCheck — Which registered actions the agent can call, and which it cannot, compared with the actions declared on the agent. Log it once at startup.
var schedulingRules: GraineSchedulingRules { get } GraineSchedulingRules — The rules for booking calls, from the session — or, before it loads, from the last session kept on the device; the defaults (no booking) when there is neither. scheduleCall checks them first.
func scheduleCall(at date: Date, reason: String? = nil) async throws -> GraineScheduledCall GraineScheduledCall GraineServiceError: scheduling_off, too_soon, too_far (on the device); outside_window, too_many_pending, identity_required, device_limit, invalid_request, rate_limited, network, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refused (from Graine); unknown when the booking was accepted but its answer could not be read Asks the agent to call this customer at date; Graine rings this device then, on the system's call screen. Waits for the session, then checks on the device before sending anything: scheduling_off when the agent does not let customers book, too_soon before schedulingRules.earliest(now:), too_far after latest(now:). reason (trimmed, cut to 120 characters) is what the agent is told the call is for; it never appears in the push. The time is sent with the device's offset and time zone; the booking is the identified customer's, or this install's when nobody is identified. Returns the booked call (status scheduled) and refreshes the chat's upcoming calls.
func scheduledCalls() async throws -> [GraineScheduledCall] [GraineScheduledCall] GraineServiceError: network, rate_limited, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refused This customer's calls still to come — this install's when nobody is identified — upcoming first. Waits for the session first.
@discardableResult func cancelScheduledCall(id: String) async throws -> GraineCallStatus GraineCallStatus GraineServiceError: not_found, network, rate_limited, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refused Calls off one of this customer's booked calls (this install's when nobody is identified); not_found for anything else. Returns the call's status afterwards — cancelled, also when Graine's answer names none.

GraineConfig

Everything the SDK needs up front, passed to GraineInApp.configure(_:name:) and kept as GraineInApp.config. A value type; only baseUrl and publishableKey are required.

Field / caseTypeDefaultMeaning
var baseUrl: String String required Graine's address: https://www.graine.ai unless self-hosted.
var publishableKey: String String required From Agent → Embed & Widgets; selects the agent. It is not a secret and cannot place a call on its own: add app:// to that agent's Allowed domains, or every request is refused.
var variables: [String: Any] [String: Any] [:] Prompt variables known at build time. identify and setVariables win over these.
var transport: GraineTransport? GraineTransport? nil Forces how the in-app call's audio travels. nil lets the dashboard's Call audio setting decide.
var appVersion: String? String? nil Lands on the call record, to tell builds apart.
var endOnBackground: Bool Bool true Ends a live in-app call when the app goes to the background (after two seconds, if it is still there). The chat also hangs up in the background and comes back with the app.
var timing: Timing GraineConfig.Timing Timing() Load timing for the engine page, for very slow networks.
var debug: Bool Bool false Logs every message between the SDK and its engine page, both ways, and the page's own console, under the subsystem ai.graine.inapp. Variables are logged as keys only and screen context as the screen's name only. The engine page can also be inspected in Safari (iOS 16.4 and later). Turn it on in debug builds.
var friction: GraineFrictionConfig? GraineFrictionConfig? nil The app's friction rules, applied over the dashboard's — for screens only the app knows about.
var fonts: [String: String] [String: String] [:] Fonts the app ships itself. The SDK downloads the design's typeface from Graine; a family named here, or one the app bundles under the family's own name, is used instead and never downloaded. Map a family to the name your app registered it under when the two differ: ["Inter": "InterVariable"].
var captureTaps: Bool Bool true Tells the agent about taps: a tap on a control with an accessibility identifier — or a button's accessibility label — reaches it as tap:<name>, any other tap as tap:screen with where it landed. At most two a second, only while a screen is set, and never a field's value. The recogniser never takes a touch from the app.
var chatSize: GraineChatSize? GraineChatSize? nil How big the chat window opens, over the dashboard's Window size: .compact above the bar, .large a sheet over most of a phone (a panel on an iPad), .full the whole screen. Nil follows the dashboard; a size passed to chat.open(size:) wins for that open.

GraineConfig.Timing

Load timing for the engine page that carries the in-app call, in milliseconds, set as GraineConfig.timing. Most apps keep the defaults.

Field / caseTypeDefaultMeaning
var stallMs: Int Int 15_000 Silence — nothing downloaded — before a load is given up on.
var bootMs: Int Int 15_000 Downloaded but still not ready after this long: the page is broken, not slow.
var hardCapMs: Int Int 120_000 Ceiling on one load attempt, however steadily it is arriving.
var retryDelaysMs: [Int] [Int] [1_000, 2_000, 4_000, 8_000, 15_000, 15_000] The waits between reloads; its length is the number of reloads before connectivity becomes failed.
var endWatchdogMs: Int Int 4_000 How long GraineVoice.end() waits for the page to confirm before ending the call locally.
var slowConnectMs: Int Int 4_000 A connect the customer has waited on this long sets GraineVoice.slowConnect ("Still connecting…").

GraineListener

Everything an agent reports, added with GraineInApp.addListener(_:); every method has a default that does nothing, so implement only what you use. Called on the main thread; listeners are held weakly, so keep your own reference.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
func onSessionReady(_ session: GraineSessionConfig) nothing — The agent's settings loaded (once per launch). GraineInApp.theme is already up to date when this is called.
func onCallState(connected: Bool, connecting: Bool) nothing — The in-app call connected, started connecting, or stopped. Called only when either value changes.
func onCaption(role: GraineRole, text: String, live: Bool) nothing — A line being said on the in-app call, again as it fills in; live is true while it is still being recognised or spoken.

func onMicDenied(reason: String) nothing — The microphone was refused — NotAllowedError when the permission is denied. Also called when a native call (calls) could not get the microphone.
func onQuality(_ quality: GraineConnectionQuality) nothing — The connection's quality, in one word. Called only when the word changes.
func onNetwork(online: Bool) nothing — The engine page saw the network go or come back.
func onReconnecting(active: Bool) nothing — The network interrupted the call and it is being re-established (true), or that is over (false). Not an end.
func onTransport(_ transport: GraineTransport, requested: GraineTransport, reason: String?, message: String?) nothing — What carries the call's audio, and why it is not the transport asked for. A reason of not_configured is a setting that never fixes itself, so it is also reported through onError.
func onConnectivity(_ state: GraineConnectivity, attempt: Int, reason: String?) nothing — The engine page loading, ready, retrying (with the reload attempt and why) or failed.
func onActionRequested(name: String) nothing — The agent asked for one of your actions.
func onActionCompleted(name: String, result: GraineActionResult) nothing — The answer the agent received for that action — your handler's, or the SDK's refused or error for an action with no handler, a throw or a timeout.
func onFriction(_ signal: GraineFrictionSignal) nothing — The customer looks stuck: on one screen, with a field outstanding, through a stretch of a live conversation. The agent is told right after; this is for the app — badge a control, count it.
func onTheme(_ tokens: GraineThemeTokens?) nothing — The brand's design tokens for the device's current appearance — when the session arrives, and again when the device switches between light and dark. Never called when the session carries no design.
func onChatMessage(_ turn: GraineChatTurn) nothing — The agent finished a message in the chat. turn.proactive is true when it spoke up without being asked — open or badge your chat for those if the customer is not looking at it.
func onError(_ message: String) nothing — Something your team must fix — a rejected key, an agent that does not accept app://, an engine page that could not load. Meant for you, never shown to the customer.
extension GraineListener — — An empty default implementation of every method above.

GraineChat

The typed conversation with an agent, on its own connection: GraineInApp.shared.chat, an ObservableObject to read on the main thread (its methods may be called from any thread and hop there). One conversation runs at a time across every agent: opening the chat ends any in-app call, starting a call closes it, a native call holds it down until it is over, and with endOnBackground it hangs up in the background and comes back with the app.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
@Published private(set) var turns: [GraineChatTurn] = [] [GraineChatTurn] — What has been said, oldest first: the customer's messages and the agent's replies, one bubble each (the last 200). Kept while the app runs.
@Published private(set) var status: GraineChatStatus = .idle GraineChatStatus — Where the connection is.
@Published private(set) var typing = false Bool — The agent is working on a reply: from the customer's message until its first words, or 30 seconds.
@Published private(set) var upcomingCalls: [GraineScheduledCall] = [] [GraineScheduledCall] — This customer's calls still to come, soonest first, at most three — the chat window's "Upcoming calls" card. Fetched when the chat opens and after the agent finishes a reply (at most every 10 seconds), only where Graine rings this app.
var online: Bool { get } Bool — Connected: a message goes now.
var awaitingFirstMessage: Bool { get } Bool — The customer has said nothing yet in this conversation, and it is not one that continues (no turn was restored): the brand's starters are offered.
private(set) var isOpen = false Bool — The customer is in the chat: open() was called and close() was not.
@Published private(set) var openedSize: GraineChatSize? GraineChatSize? — The size the current open asked for (open(size:)), until close(); nil follows GraineConfig.chatSize, then the dashboard's. Moving to the call and back keeps it.
func open(size: GraineChatSize? = nil) nothing — The customer is in the chat: connect, and stay connected. A mounted GraineAgentBar moves to the chat (where the agent offers one) and draws it at size until close(); nil follows GraineConfig.chatSize, then the dashboard's. Ends any in-app call and closes other agents' chats. A dropped connection is made again 1, 2, 4, 8, 15 and 15 seconds apart, then the status is offline until the customer sends something or you call retry().
func close() nothing — The customer left: the chat hangs up and stays down. What was said stays on screen.
func send(_ text: String) nothing — Sends a message. It is shown at once and sent now, or as soon as the chat is connected (opening and connecting it if needed). Empty text is ignored. Up to 20 messages wait while the chat is down; older ones are marked failed.
func retry() nothing — Connects now, and sends what could not be sent.
func newConversation() async throws nothing GraineServiceError: device_limit, network, … Starts a fresh thread: the chat hangs up, Graine lets go of the conversation it kept for this agent and customer, the chat on screen clears and — when the customer was in the chat — a fresh chat opens with the welcome and the starters. Memories are untouched. With nobody identified only the screen clears. On a refusal the chat is as it was, connected again. GraineChatView's header offers it while it shows an earlier conversation.
func refreshUpcomingCalls() nothing — Fetches the upcoming calls again — after booking one elsewhere, say.
func cancelUpcomingCall(id: String) nothing — Cancels one of the card's calls. Its row says "Cancelling…" until Graine has it, then goes; a failure leaves the row marked so the customer can try again. Nothing is thrown.

The in-app voice call: a page Graine hosts, in a web view the SDK owns (one invisible point big), so audio fixes reach your app without a release — reached as GraineInApp.shared.voice and driven for you by GraineAgentBar. An ObservableObject; every method belongs on the main thread, and one called from elsewhere hops there.

Say so ("Still connecting…"). Cleared the moment it lands or they stop waiting.
@Published private(set) var callFailed = false Bool — The last start could not be connected on either transport. Not a setting to fix — the network may be better in a moment, so start() simply tries again. Cleared by a start, an answered call, end() and detach().

var phase: GrainePhase { get } GrainePhase — What the call is doing in one word — idle, connecting, reconnecting, thinking, speaking or listening — for an app that draws its own bar. Draw GraineLoader(moment: "thinking") for thinking.
func attach(to view: UIView) nothing — Mounts the engine in that view — pass your key window, not a view a screen owns — and loads the page idle: nothing registered, nothing dialled, no microphone, so a later start() connects quickly. Attaching somewhere new moves the engine and ends any call in progress.
func attach() nothing — Mounts the engine in the app's key window. Call it once a window exists — from a view's onAppear, say; with no window yet it reports through onError and does nothing.
func detach() nothing — Removes the engine, hanging up first: a call never outlives its UI.
func start() nothing — Places the call. Asks for the microphone first if the app does not hold it; refused, no call is placed and onMicDenied is called. A start before the page is ready is held and placed when it is. Ends any other conversation — another agent's call, every chat. Refused through onError when the engine is not attached or a native call (calls) is live.
func end() nothing — Hangs up. If the page does not confirm within Timing.endWatchdogMs (4 s), the call is ended locally — state, onEnded, and a reload that drops the audio. A start that was only being held is simply cancelled.
func setMuted(_ value: Bool) nothing — Stops (or resumes) sending the customer's voice without ending the call.
func answerWidget(widgetId: String, data: [String: Any], summary: String) nothing — The customer answered a component the agent drew. summary is the sentence the agent hears ("Let's compare the two plans."); without it the tap lands and the conversation does not move. GraineWidgetView does this itself.
func reportEvent(_ name: String, detail: String? = nil, data: [String: Any] = [:]) nothing — Something the agent may want to speak up about. Only during a call — otherwise it is dropped, so it never opens the next conversation. The current screen is sent first. data may carry quiet, cooldown_seconds and max_per_session, which pace the agent.
func retry() nothing — Reloads the engine page and starts the reload ladder over — for a "Try again" button.
