Reached as GraineInApp.shared.calls (one object for the whole app, one call at a time); an ObservableObject on the main thread whose methods hop there when called elsewhere.

@Published private(set) var missedCall: GraineMissedCall? GraineMissedCall? — The ring nobody answered, kept for 30 seconds after the call is over so a call screen can say "Missed call" and offer callBack() — or until the customer calls back, dismissMissedCall() is called, or another call rings or is placed.
var showsCallScreen: Bool { get } Bool — Whether a call screen has something to show: a call, its last second, or a missed ring to call back.
private(set) var config = GraineCallsConfig() GraineCallsConfig — The configuration in force.
func configure(_ config: GraineCallsConfig) nothing — How calls ring and what they show. Call once, at launch, before enableVoIPPushes.
func enableVoIPPushes(onToken: ((String?) -> Void)? = nil) nothing — Receive your agent's calls as VoIP pushes. Call it at launch, every launch: iOS wakes a terminated app for a push and delivers it once this has run. Every VoIP push is reported to CallKit before its completion runs, as iOS requires. onToken gets the device's VoIP token as hex — at once when already known, again when it changes, nil when iOS invalidates it — for your own server. When the workspace has hosted ringing (Graine rings this app), the SDK registers the token with Graine itself, for every configured agent whose workspace rings iOS — on a new token, a new signed-in customer, a new time zone or app version, and otherwise at most once a day — and reports what became of every ring.
func addListener(_ listener: GraineCallsListener) nothing — Hear about calls. Held weakly; called on the main thread.
func removeListener(_ listener: GraineCallsListener) nothing — Stops reporting to that listener.
@discardableResult func startCall(reason: String? = nil, variables: [String: Any] = [:], agent: String? = nil) -> String? String? — The customer calls the agent. The agent hears who_called = "customer" and call_reason (reason), with variables (masked on the device) over the SDK's own; a call carries at most 12 variables, names up to 40 characters, values up to 200, about 1 KB in all. agent names which configured agent to call; nil is the default. Returns the call's id — "call_" and a lowercase UUID — or nil when a call is already live or no agent has that name. Asks for the microphone first if the app does not hold it; refused, the call ends failed and onMicDenied is called. Ends any in-app (voice) call.
func reportIncomingCall(payload: [AnyHashable: Any], completion: (() -> Void)? = nil) nothing — For an app with its own PKPushRegistry: hands over a VoIP push's payload. It is reported to CallKit at once — before completion runs, as iOS requires — even when it is not a usable agent call or a call is already live; then it is ended at once, a live call is never disturbed, and a different call arriving mid-call is reported missed. The payload carries type: "agent_call" and a call_id, and optionally reason, caller_name, variables, hosted and agent_id (the agent the ring is for); the keys may sit under data.
func voipTokenUpdated(_ token: String?) nothing — For an app with its own PKPushRegistry: the VoIP token (hex, or nil once invalidated), handled as enableVoIPPushes would handle it — registered with Graine where Graine rings this app.
func answer() nothing — Answers the ringing call from your own screen; the system's call screen answers by itself. The call is reported answered at once; if the microphone is then refused, or its prompt goes unanswered for a minute, the call ends failed.
func end() nothing — Hangs up — or declines, while it rings.
func setMuted(_ value: Bool) nothing — Stops (or resumes) sending the customer's voice without ending the call; the system's call screen shows it too.
func setSpeaker(_ on: Bool) nothing — The loudspeaker (true) or the earpiece or headset (false). A call starts on the earpiece, or a connected headset.
@discardableResult func callBack() -> String? String? — Returns the missed call: the customer calls the agent that rang, with the missed call's reason (or returning_missed_call) as call_reason. The new call's id, or nil when there is nothing to return or a call is live.
func dismissMissedCall() nothing — The customer has seen the missed call: the screen can go.
func providerDidReset(_ provider: CXProvider) nothing — CallKit's callback when the system resets every call; the SDK ends its call. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, perform action: CXStartCallAction) nothing — CallKit's callback for a call being placed; the SDK opens the conversation. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, perform action: CXAnswerCallAction) nothing — CallKit's callback for an answer; the SDK answers at once and settles the microphone after. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, perform action: CXEndCallAction) nothing — CallKit's callback for a hang-up or decline. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, perform action: CXSetMutedCallAction) nothing — CallKit's callback for mute from the system's call screen. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, perform action: CXSetHeldCallAction) nothing — CallKit's callback for hold; an agent call is never put on hold, so the action fails and the system offers "End & Accept" instead. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, didActivate audioSession: AVAudioSession) nothing — CallKit's callback when the system hands over the audio; the call's audio starts here. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, didDeactivate audioSession: AVAudioSession) nothing — CallKit's callback when the system takes the audio back; the app's own audio session is restored after the call. Apps do not call it.
func provider(_ provider: CXProvider, timedOutPerforming action: CXAction) nothing — CallKit's callback for an action that timed out; logged. Apps do not call it.
func pushRegistry(_ registry: PKPushRegistry, didUpdate pushCredentials: PKPushCredentials, for type: PKPushType) nothing — PushKit's callback with a new VoIP token, handled as described for enableVoIPPushes. Apps do not call it.
func pushRegistry(_ registry: PKPushRegistry, didInvalidatePushTokenFor type: PKPushType) nothing — PushKit's callback when the VoIP token is invalidated; onToken gets nil. Apps do not call it.
func pushRegistry(_ registry: PKPushRegistry, didReceiveIncomingPushWith payload: PKPushPayload, for type: PKPushType, completion: @escaping () -> Void) nothing — PushKit's callback with a VoIP push, passed to reportIncomingCall(payload:completion:). Apps do not call it.

Field / caseTypeDefaultMeaning
var displayName: String String "" The name a call rings with and shows on the call screen — your agent's, or your brand's. Empty: the agent's call name from the dashboard, else your app's name. With one agent configured a non-empty value wins; with several, each agent's dashboard call name comes first, so a ring says who is calling. A push's caller_name wins for its own call.

var includesCallsInRecents: Bool Bool false List the calls in the Phone app's Recents.
var ringTimeout: TimeInterval TimeInterval 30 Seconds an agent's call rings before it is missed (at least 1). A ring Graine sent lasts the agent's ring timeout from the dashboard instead.
init(displayName: String = "", ringtoneSound: String? = nil, iconTemplateImageData: Data? = nil, includesCallsInRecents: Bool = false, ringTimeout: TimeInterval = 30) initialiser — Builds a calls configuration.

GraineCallView

A ready call screen for while your app is in the foreground, drawn in the design of the agent the call is with; the system's own call screen covers the lock screen and the background. A SwiftUI view — present it over your UI, for example .fullScreenCover(isPresented: .constant(calls.showsCallScreen)) { GraineCallView() }.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
init(calls: GraineCalls? = nil) GraineCallView — The calls to draw; GraineInApp.shared.calls when nil, so an agent must be configured. The screen draws every moment of a call: a call Graine rang at a booked time ringing ("Scheduled call") and any other ring ("Incoming call"), each with Decline and Answer; connecting ("Connecting…"); on the call — the timer (with "· Muted" while muted), or "Muted", "Speaking" or "Listening" when the design has no timer, the line being said, and Mute, Speaker and End in the design's order; ended ("Call ended", "Call failed" or "Declined", the controls dimmed); and missed ("Missed call") with Close and Call back, for 30 seconds. The avatar is the brand's logo, its launcher glyph or the call name's initial; a ring pulses out while it rings and the avatar breathes while the agent speaks, not under Reduce Motion. A push that woke a closed app draws from the last session kept on the device.
var body: some View some View — SwiftUI's view body; apps do not call it.

GraineCallsHost

The bridge the React Native and Flutter packages use to drive GraineCalls with JSON-safe values (strings, numbers, booleans, null, lists and string-keyed maps); apps on native iOS do not call it — GraineInApp.shared.calls is the Swift API. Reached as GraineCallsHost.shared; it runs on the main thread, and configure, restore, snapshot, startCall, installId and addSink wait for their answer when called from another thread.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
@objc static let shared = GraineCallsHost() GraineCallsHost — The one host per process. Used by the React Native and Flutter bridges.
typealias Sink = (_ event: String, _ payload: [String: Any]) -> Void — — Receives every event on the main thread: its name — state (the snapshot, at most once per turn of the main loop), outcome, incoming, voipToken or action — and its payload.
@objc @discardableResult func restore() -> Bool Bool — At launch, before any JavaScript or Dart runs: applies the options the last configure kept, and enables VoIP pushes again if they were, so a push that woke a terminated app rings. True when something was restored; false when nothing was kept or this launch is already configured.
func configure(_ options: [String: Any]?) throws nothing GraineCallsHostError: invalid_options Configures the calls and keeps the options for the next cold start; the first call makes the SDK instance. Options: publishableKey and displayName (required), baseUrl, ringtoneSound, ringTimeoutMs (30,000 by default), appVersion, callScreen ("sdk" or "app"), debug, android, ios (iconTemplate, includesCallsInRecents) and agents (more agents by name, each {publishableKey, baseUrl?}). Unknown keys are ignored; a known key of the wrong type is refused, naming it. A new key, base URL or debug setting takes effect at the next launch.
func snapshot() -> [String: Any] [String: Any] — The call as a call screen draws it, every key always present: state, callId, direction, reason, callerName, muted, speakerOn, agentSpeaking, caption, connectedAt (milliseconds since the epoch), error and agent.
func enableVoIPPushes() nothing — Receive the agent's calls as VoIP pushes, now and at every launch after. The token arrives as a voipToken event — again on every call, the last one known.
func handlePush(_ data: [String: Any]?) -> Bool Bool — Always false on iOS, where a VoIP push reaches PushKit and the SDK directly. It exists for the Android side of the bridges.
func startCall(_ options: [String: Any]?) -> String? String? — The customer calls the agent: {reason?, variables?, agent?}. The call's id, or nil when not configured, a call is live, or no agent has that name.
func answer() nothing — Answers the ringing call.
func decline() nothing — Declines the ringing call (on iOS, end while it rings); does nothing otherwise.
func end() nothing — Hangs up.
func setMuted(_ muted: Bool) nothing — Mutes or unmutes the customer.
func setSpeaker(_ on: Bool) nothing — The loudspeaker or the earpiece.
func setIdentity(_ traits: [String: Any]?) nothing — Who is signed in (GraineInApp.identify); nil on sign-out. Held until the instance exists.
func setMemory(_ enabled: Bool) nothing — The current customer's memory choice (GraineInApp.setMemory). Held until the instance exists.
func installId() -> String? String? — This install's id, kept in the Keychain — the one the native calls send, so a device is one install whichever layer speaks. Nil before configure or restore.
func setVariables(_ values: [String: Any]?) nothing — The runtime variables become exactly this map: a key the last map set and this one leaves out is removed. Reaches every agent.
func setScreen(_ screen: [String: Any]?) nothing — The screen, as {screen, title?, journey?, fields?, error?, data?, availableActions?}; nil, or no screen name, for none.
func setActions(_ names: [String], sink: Int?) nothing — The actions the caller answers, and its sink's token: each request for one is sent as an action event to the sink that last listed a non-empty set, and waits for resolveAction within the SDK's six seconds. Names no longer listed are unregistered.
func resolveAction(_ requestId: String, result: [String: Any]?) nothing — The answer to an action request: {status: "ok" | "refused" | "error", message?, data?}. The first answer wins.
func addSink(_ sink: @escaping Sink) -> Int Int — Starts receiving events; returns the sink's token. Outcomes and rings that came while nothing listened (the last 20) are delivered to the first sink at once.
func removeSink(_ token: Int) nothing — Stops that sink. Action requests it had not answered are refused.

GraineMasking

What never leaves the device unmasked: PAN, email, card, Indian mobile and Aadhaar numbers are replaced, in that order, in what the app reports — screens, events, traits and runtime variables — before it is sent. Static members, safe from any thread; masking is a set of rules, not a guarantee.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
static func mask(_ input: String) -> String String — Replaces identifiers in one string with [PAN], [EMAIL], [CARD], [PHONE] and [AADHAAR], then applies the app's own rules.
static func addRule(_ pattern: NSRegularExpression, token: String = "[REDACTED]") nothing — A rule for a field shape only your app knows — an account number, a policy id. Registered for the whole app, once at startup; every match is replaced. token is a template: $1 refers to a capture group.
@discardableResult static func addRule(pattern: String, token: String = "[REDACTED]") -> Bool Bool — The same, from a pattern string. Returns false, and adds nothing, when the pattern does not compile.
static func clearCustomRules() nothing — Removes the app's own rules. For tests only.
static func deep(_ value: Any?) -> Any Any — Masks every string anywhere inside a JSON value. Keys are not masked; numbers and other non-string values are returned untouched.

13.5Android — ai.graine:inapp-android 0.7.0

Kotlin, usable from Java (overloads and static companions are generated). Every public declaration of the library is listed below, except Android framework overrides inside the SDK's own views, activities and services (such as onCreate or onLayout), which are not for apps to call. Errors from requests to Graine arrive in the callback's error as a GraineError — never thrown.

GraineInApp

class GraineInApp private constructor(internal val application: Application, val config: GraineConfig, val name: String, internal val env: AgentEnv) — The agent. Create it once in Application.onCreate with GraineInApp.init(application, config) and reach it anywhere with GraineInApp.get(). Every member is called on the main thread; callbacks arrive on the main thread with exactly one of value and error set.

FieldTypeDefaultMeaning
configGraineConfigrequired
nameStringrequiredThis agent's name: DEFAULT unless init() was given another.

fun scheduledCalls(done: GraineCallback<List<GraineScheduledCall>>)nothingIn the callback's error (GraineError): network, rate_limited, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refusedThe calls booked for the signed-in user (or this install) that are still to come, soonest first.
fun cancelScheduledCall(id: String, done: GraineCallback<GraineCallStatus>? = null)nothingIn the callback's error (GraineError): not_found, network, rate_limited, unavailableCancel a booked call — only one booked for this user or install.

GraineConfig

data class GraineConfig @JvmOverloads constructor(…) — How the SDK starts: the base URL (https://www.graine.ai), the agent's publishable key, and options. Pass it to GraineInApp.init.

FieldTypeDefaultMeaning

publishableKeyStringrequiredFrom Agent → Embed & Widgets.

endOnBackgroundBooleantrueEnd a live call when the app goes to the background.

debugBooleanfalseLog every message across the bridge, both ways, and the engine page's own console, to logcat under the tag "Graine".

13.6Flutter — graine_inapp 0.7.0

Dart; everything package:graine_inapp/graine_inapp.dart exports. Requests to Graine throw GraineException; state objects are ChangeNotifiers and ValueListenables; call them on the UI isolate.

GraineInApp

The in-app agent: one instance per publishable key, configured with GraineInApp.init(config) before runApp and reached afterwards as GraineInApp.instance (or GraineInApp.named('support') for an agent configured under a name). Accessing instance before init throws StateError. It is a WidgetsBindingObserver. Use it on the main (UI) isolate only.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
static const String defaultName = 'default'String—The name of the default agent: the one init configures when given no name, which instance returns and every view draws unless handed another.
static GraineInApp init(GraineConfig config, {String name = defaultName})GraineInApp—Configures an agent and starts fetching its configuration at once. Call it before runApp or in your first widget; it initialises the Flutter binding itself. Without a name it is the default agent. The name is trimmed, and an empty name is the default agent. A later call with a name already configured returns that agent unchanged (the new config is not applied).
static GraineInApp? named(String name)GraineInApp?—The agent configured under name (trimmed; empty means the default agent), or null.
static Map<String, GraineInApp> get allMap<String, GraineInApp>—Every configured agent, by name, in the order they were configured. Unmodifiable.
static GraineInApp get instanceGraineInAppStateError before initThe default agent: the one configured without a name, or, in an app that named every agent, the first one configured.
static GraineInApp? get maybeInstanceGraineInApp?—The default agent, or null before init. Use it to ask whether the SDK has been configured.

With install: true it joins the app's agents under name; otherwise it shares nothing with them.

final GraineConfig configGraineConfig—The configuration this agent was initialised with.
final String nameString—The name this agent was configured under; defaultName for the default agent.
late final GraineVoice voiceGraineVoice—This agent's voice call. GraineEngine attaches it; voice.start() places a call.
late final GraineComponents componentsGraineComponents—The components the agent draws (from the call or the chat), as state a GraineWidgetView renders.
GraineChatSession get chatGraineChatSession—This agent's text chat, on its own connection; created on first use. GraineAgentBar and GraineChat open it while the customer is in it and close it when they leave; an app drawing its own chat calls open() and close() itself. Opening it ends any other agent's call and closes its chat.
void addListener(GraineListener l)nothing—Adds a listener for this agent's events. It is kept until removed; adding the same object twice has no further effect. A listener that throws is logged and does not stop the others.
void removeListener(GraineListener l)nothing—Removes a listener.
void identify(Map<String, Object?>? traits, {bool? memory})nothing—Who is signed in. Traits become prompt variables, masked on the device, and land on the call record — except the one trait the agent's Identity setting names (user_id unless it names email, phone or a custom trait), which is kept raw and sent only where Graine needs it to recognise the user, never as a prompt variable or in the screen context. A placeholder (such as "guest", "null" or an already-masked "[EMAIL]"), null, a boolean or a fraction identifies nobody: that conversation is anonymous, with no memory. memory: false: this user's conversations are neither remembered nor recalled; the choice is kept on the device for this user, and when left out their last choice stands (on until they make one). Identity is fixed per conversation: a change reaches the next one. null signs out: Graine is told this device is no longer the user's, a chat open for them ends and its transcript is cleared, and later conversations are anonymous. A different user signing in without a sign-out first signs the previous one out the same way. One user for the whole app: every agent the app configured hears it (each keeps the trait its own Identity setting names), and the native call engine receives it too.
void setMemory(bool enabled)nothing—Whether the current user's conversations are remembered — the same as identify(currentTraits, memory: enabled). Kept on the device for that user (for an anonymous user, for this run only). Applies to every agent and reaches the native call engine.
Future<bool> memoryEnabled()Future<bool>—The current user's memory choice: true unless they turned it off. Waits for the agent's configuration and the choices kept on the device.
Future<int> forgetMemory()Future<int> — how many memories were deletedGraineException: identityRequired (checked on the device first), deviceLimit, rateLimited, unavailable, invalidKey, originRefused, network, unknownDeletes everything this agent's memory holds about the identified user. Allowed only from a device that is theirs. Completes with the number deleted (0 when Graine does not say).
Future<List<GraineMemory>> memories()Future<List<GraineMemory>>GraineException: identityRequired (checked on the device first), deviceLimit, rateLimited, unavailable, invalidKey, originRefused, network, unknownWhat this agent remembers about the identified user, already redacted, in Graine's order: newest first, at most 100. For a "what you remember about me" screen. Only from a device that is theirs.
Future<String> get installIdFuture<String>—This install's id: a UUID made on the app's first launch and kept by the platform (the Keychain on iOS, surviving reinstalls; storage excluded from backups on Android). The same id the native call engine sends, and the same for every agent. Graine counts a user's devices by it; the agent never sees it. Where there is no platform side (a test, a desktop build) it is a random UUID kept in memory for the run.
GraineSchedulingRules get schedulingRulesGraineSchedulingRules—What the agent lets users book, and how Graine rings, from the agent's configuration. No request. Before the configuration loads, and from a server that says nothing, the defaults — which allow no booking.
Future<GraineScheduledCall> scheduleCall({required DateTime at, String? reason})Future<GraineScheduledCall> — the booked call, status scheduledGraineException — on the device: invalidRequest, schedulingOff, tooSoon, tooFar; from Graine: outsideWindow, tooManyPending, identityRequired, deviceLimit, invalidRequest, rateLimited, unavailable, invalidKey, originRefused, network; unknown (codeName "bad_response") when the booking is not confirmedBooks a call from the agent at at ("call me tomorrow at 6"). The agent rings this user's devices (with nobody identified, this install) through the app. reason is trimmed, at most 120 characters, kept with the call for the agent, and never put in the push that rings it. Checks made on the device before the booking request is sent: a reason over 120 characters (invalidRequest, checked first); then, once the agent's configuration has loaded, schedulingOff when users may not book, tooSoon before schedulingRules.earliest(now) and tooFar after schedulingRules.latest(now), where now is the device clock. The time is sent as ISO-8601 with the device's offset. An open chat's Upcoming calls card shows the booking at once.
Future<List<GraineScheduledCall>> scheduledCalls()Future<List<GraineScheduledCall>>GraineException: rateLimited, unavailable, invalidKey, originRefused, network, notFound (a server with no booked calls to list), unknownThis user's calls (with nobody identified, this install's), in Graine's order: upcoming first. Entries that are not calls are skipped.
Future<GraineCallStatus> cancelScheduledCall(String id)Future<GraineCallStatus> — the call's status afterwardsGraineException: invalidRequest (an empty id, on the device), notFound (not this user's or install's), rateLimited, unavailable, invalidKey, originRefused, network, unknownCancels one of this user's booked calls. The id is trimmed. Completes with the status Graine reports afterwards — GraineCallStatus.cancelled when it does not say. An open chat's Upcoming calls card drops the call.
void setVariables(Map<String, Object?>? values)nothing—Prompt variables from the app's own data, for this agent. Merged into what is there: null under a key removes it; null for the whole map clears them all. Values become strings (an integer never gains ".0"; maps and lists are dropped) and are masked on the device. They reach the next conversation, and a ready engine page receives them at once.
Map<String, String> currentVariables()Map<String, String>—Every variable the agent will receive, merged in precedence order: the dashboard's defaults, then GraineConfig.variables, then setVariables, then the traits from identify (without the identifying trait once the configuration has loaded).
void setScreen(GraineScreen? next)nothing—What the customer is looking at; null forgets it. Call it on every meaningful change. Values are masked on the device before they leave, and an unchanged screen is not resent. The first change goes out at once; a burst after it is coalesced into one more update at the end of a 400 ms window, so the agent's opening line is never a screen behind. The screen is the app's: every agent hears it and tells its own conversation while one is live. A new screen id starts a new visit for friction detection.
void updateField(GraineField field)nothing—Replaces the current screen's field of the same name, or adds it after the others. Does nothing before a screen is set (the next setScreen carries the field itself) or for a field with an empty name.
void removeField(String name)nothing—Removes a field from the current screen. Does nothing if no screen is set or the field was never reported.
void clearScreen([String? screenId])nothing—Forgets the screen, but only if screenId (when given) is still the current screen's id. Call it from a screen's cleanup: a navigator keeps the old screen through its exit transition, and an unconditional setScreen(null) there would wipe the screen that has just replaced it.
void track(String name, [Map<String, Object?> data = const <String, Object?>{}])nothing—A product event the agent is told about without being interrupted. It rides the next context update; the last ten events are kept. Every agent records it. An empty name is ignored.
void tap(String name)nothing—The customer tapped a control you name: recorded as "tap:<name>" in the recent events (the name cut to one line of at most 40 characters), so the agent knows what they just did. Context, not news: it goes out at the end of the 400 ms window. Every agent records it. An empty name is ignored.
void captureTap({required double x, required double y, String? label})nothing—A tap anywhere in the app. GraineEngine reports every tap it sees; an app with its own gesture layer may call it too. On a control with an accessibility label it is recorded as "tap:<label>" (one line, at most 40 characters); elsewhere as "tap:screen" with x and y in logical pixels. Recorded only by agents with GraineConfig.captureTaps on that have a screen set, and at most two taps a second across the app. Context, not news: it rides the next update.
void configureFriction(FrictionConfig? override)nothing—Replaces the app's layer of friction rules (the layer GraineConfig.friction set). Safe at any time. The rules in force become the defaults, then the dashboard's, then override.
FrictionRules get frictionRulesFrictionRules—The friction rules in force now: the defaults, the dashboard's, then the app's.
void noteInteraction()nothing—The customer did something that is not a field edit — scrolled a list, opened a picker. Restarts every agent's idle clock. Field edits do not count.
void Function() registerAction(String name, GraineActionHandler handler)void Function() — unregisters it—Something the agent can do in the app, for this agent. Declare the same action on the agent in the dashboard: a handler with no declaration is never offered, and a declaration with no handler is refused. The handler may answer synchronously or with a Future and must answer within six seconds, or the agent is told it was not done; returning null means ok, and a throw is answered as error. Registering a name again replaces its handler. The returned function unregisters it, if it is still the one registered.
Map<String, List<String>> checkActions()Map<String, List<String>>—Compares what this build registered with what the agent declares: usable (both), undeclared (registered, not declared on the agent), unhandled (declared, not registered). Declarations come from the agent's configuration, so read it after the session has loaded; log it once at startup.
Future<ActionResult> executeAction(String name, Map<String, Object?> args)Future<ActionResult>—Runs one registered action exactly as the agent would, against the six-second deadline, and reports onActionRequested and onActionCompleted to listeners. Always completes: an unknown name answers refused; a throw or a timeout answers error.
Map<String, Object?>? get pendingWidgetMap<String, Object?>?—The component the agent drew that is still waiting to be answered, as Graine sent it, so a view mounted later can still draw it. Cleared when it is answered or dismissed, and when a new call starts.
void clearPendingWidget()nothing—Forgets the retained component.
SessionConfig? get sessionSessionConfig?—What the dashboard says about this agent; null until it has loaded.
ValueListenable<SessionConfig?> get sessionListenableValueListenable<SessionConfig?>—The session, for a widget that rebuilds when it arrives.
Future<SessionConfig?> loadSession()Future<SessionConfig?>—Fetches the agent's configuration once; concurrent callers share one request, and a failure is retried by the next caller. Completes with null on failure, which is also reported through GraineListener.onError. init calls it.
ResolvedDesign? get designResolvedDesign?—The design the brand chose in the dashboard, with both token sets. Null until the session loads, and from a server that predates designs.
ThemeTokens? get tokensThemeTokens?—The tokens to draw with right now: the brand's fixed scheme, else the device's light or dark, re-picked when the device switches. Null without a design. For an app drawing its own UI; the SDK's widgets pick for themselves.
ValueListenable<ThemeTokens?> get tokensListenableValueListenable<ThemeTokens?>—The tokens, for a widget that rebuilds when they change.
@override void didChangePlatformBrightness()nothing—Lifecycle callback: the device switched between light and dark, so the tokens are picked again. Called by Flutter; apps do not call it.
ValueListenable<Map<String, String>> get fontFacesValueListenable<Map<String, String>>—The design's typefaces the SDK has loaded: family|weight (the design's family at the weight it really has) → the family name the face is registered under, for example "DM Sans|700" → "Graine-DMSans-700". Empty until one loads, and for "system", which is never fetched. To draw your own UI in the brand's typeface, set fontFamily to the registered name with FontWeight.normal: a loaded face is its weight.
Future<void> loadDesignFonts(ResolvedDesign? design)Future<void>—Fetches and registers the faces design draws with. The SDK does this for the session's design itself; call it for a design you hand a widget directly. Families listed in GraineConfig.fonts are the app's own and are never fetched. Safe to call again: each face is fetched once.
bool get foregroundbool—Whether the app is in the foreground, as the lifecycle last reported.
@override void didChangeAppLifecycleState(AppLifecycleState state)nothing—Lifecycle callback: resumed is the foreground; inactive is ignored (iOS reports it for the app switcher, a pulled-down notification and the microphone permission dialog); anything else is the background. Called by Flutter; apps do not call it.
@visibleForTesting void setForegroundForTesting(bool foreground)nothing—For tests only: what the lifecycle callback calls.
@visibleForTesting void dispose()nothing—For tests only: stops every timer, detaches the engine, closes the chat and removes the agent from the app's agents. An app keeps its agents for its lifetime.

GraineConfig

Everything the SDK needs up front, passed to GraineInApp.init. Immutable.

Field / caseTypeDefaultMeaning
const GraineConfig({required this.baseUrl, required this.publishableKey, this.variables = const <String, Object?>{}, this.transport, this.appVersion, this.endOnBackground = true, this.timing = const GraineTiming(), this.debug = false, this.friction, this.requestMicrophone, this.fonts = const <String>[], this.captureTaps = true, this.chatSize})——The constructor.
final String baseUrlStringrequired"https://www.graine.ai" unless self-hosted.
final String publishableKeyStringrequiredFrom Agent → Embed & Widgets. Selects the agent. It is not a secret and cannot place a call on its own: add app:// to that agent's Allowed domains, or every request is refused.
final Map<String, Object?> variablesMap<String, Object?>emptyPrompt variables known at build time. The dashboard's defaults sit under them; setVariables and identify win over them. Unlike runtime variables and traits, the SDK does not mask these.
final Transport? transportTransport?nullForces a transport. Null lets the dashboard's Call audio setting decide.
final String? appVersionString?nullLands on the call record and in the screen context, to tell builds apart.
final bool endOnBackgroundbooltrueEnds a live call, and hangs up a connected chat, once the app has been in the background for two seconds (a moment away, such as a permission dialog, does not count). The chat reconnects when the app returns, if the customer is still in it. You want it on.
final GraineTiming timingGraineTimingGraineTiming()The page-load watchdog, retry ladder, end-call watchdog and "Still connecting…" threshold.
final bool debugboolfalseLogs, prefixed "[Graine]", every message across the engine bridge both ways, the chat's frames and the engine page's console. Outgoing variables and screen context are logged by key names and screen id only; incoming messages are logged as received, cut to 600 characters. Turn it on in debug builds.
final FrictionConfig? frictionFrictionConfig?nullThis app's layer of friction rules, over the dashboard's. Most apps set nothing here.
final Future<bool> Function()? requestMicrophoneFuture<bool> Function()?nullMakes sure the app holds the microphone before a call opens; this package has no permission plugin of its own, so pass the one the app already uses (for example () async => (await Permission.microphone.request()).isGranted). Called by GraineVoice.start() — and so by the bar's microphone button and GraineLauncher — before the call is placed. false: no call is opened and onMicDenied("NotAllowedError") is reported. If it throws, the error is logged and the call is attempted anyway. Null: the SDK assumes the app asked already; if it did not, the engine reports the refusal.
final List<String> fontsList<String>emptyThe font families the app bundles itself, by the family name its pubspec declares. The SDK fetches the brand's typeface by itself; a family listed here is the app's own copy, wins over the download and is never fetched. Empty: the SDK fetches every family the design uses, drawing the platform font until each arrives.
final bool captureTapsbooltrueTells the agent what the customer taps while a screen is set: a tap on a control with an accessibility label (Semantics(label: …)) as "tap:<label>", anywhere else as "tap:screen" with the position — in the recent events, at most two a second, masked like everything else. GraineEngine (given a child) sees the taps.
final GraineChatSize? chatSizeGraineChatSize?nullHow big the chat window opens, over the dashboard's Window size: compact above the bar, large a sheet over most of a phone (a panel on a tablet), full the whole screen. Null follows the dashboard; a size passed to GraineChat.open wins for that open.

GraineTiming

Load and connect timing, for an app used on very slow networks. Passed as GraineConfig.timing; all values in milliseconds.

Field / caseTypeDefaultMeaning
const GraineTiming({this.stallMs = 15000, this.bootMs = 15000, this.hardCapMs = 120000, this.retryDelaysMs = const <int>[1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 15000, 15000], this.endWatchdogMs = 4000, this.slowConnectMs = 4000})——The constructor.
final int stallMsint15000Silence — nothing downloaded — before a page load is given up on and retried.
final int bootMsint15000Downloaded but still not ready after this long: the page is broken, not slow.
final int hardCapMsint120000The ceiling on one load attempt, however steadily it is arriving.
final List<int> retryDelaysMsList<int>1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 15 sThe whole retry ladder, each delay jittered by ±25%. Its length is the number of reloads before the SDK gives up and reports GraineConnectivity.failed. The chat's reconnect backoff uses the same ladder.
final int endWatchdogMsint4000How long an end-call may go unconfirmed before the call is torn down locally.
final int slowConnectMsint4000How long a connect the customer is waiting on runs before slowConnect turns true ("Still connecting…").

GraineListener

Everything an agent reports. An abstract mixin class: use it with extends or with; every method has an empty default, so override only what you use. Register it with GraineInApp.addListener. Delivered on the main isolate.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
void onSessionReady(SessionConfig session) {}nothing—The agent's configuration has loaded.
void onCallState(bool connected, bool connecting) {}nothing—The voice call connected, started connecting, or stopped. Also fires when a connect attempt ends because nothing could carry the call.
void onCaption(Role role, String text, bool live) {}nothing—A line of the voice call: repeated with live: true as it fills in, then once settled. The chat's lines are in GraineChatSession.turns.
void onWidget(Map<String, Object?> widget) {}nothing—The agent drew a component, in the call or the chat, as Graine sent it. GraineComponents already holds it for GraineWidgetView; an app drawing its own answers it with GraineVoice.answerWidget (call) or GraineChatSession.answerWidget (chat).
void onWidgetPending(Map<String, Object?> hint) {}nothing—A component is on its way and its content is loading; the hint carries its widget_id and kind when Graine gives them.
void onEnded() {}nothing—The voice call is over, however it ended (including a hang-up the engine never confirmed). Once per call.
void onMicDenied(String reason) {}nothing—The microphone was refused: "NotAllowedError" when requestMicrophone answered false (or the engine asked for it after that), otherwise the engine's reason, such as "NotFoundError".
void onQuality(ConnectionQuality quality) {}nothing—One word for the connection; fires only when the word changes. lost when the network goes; unknown when a call ends.
void onNetwork(bool online) {}nothing—The engine page's view of the network changed.
void onReconnecting(bool active) {}nothing—The network interrupted the call and it is being re-established (true), or that is over (false). Not an end.
void onTransport(Transport transport, Transport requested, String? reason, String? message) {}nothing—Which transport carries the call, which was asked for, and why they differ. With reason "not_configured", message is also reported to onError and held as GraineVoice.error.
void onConnectivity(GraineConnectivity state, int attempt, String? reason) {}nothing—The engine page is loading, ready, retrying or has failed. attempt is the number of reloads so far; reason is a short word such as "stalled", "boot_timeout", "load_cap" or "session".
void onActionRequested(String name) {}nothing—The agent asked the app to run an action; fires before the handler runs.
void onActionCompleted(String name, ActionResult result) {}nothing—The answer the agent was given for that action.
void onFriction(FrictionSignal signal) {}nothing—The customer looks stuck on a step (stalled_on_step): on one screen, with a field outstanding, through a stretch of a live conversation. The conversation is told at the same moment; this is for the app — badge a control, count it.
void onAgentVolunteered(String text) {}nothing—In the chat, the agent spoke without being asked — its welcome, or something it noticed on screen; text is the turn's first words. Open the chat if it is closed.
void onError(String message) {}nothing—Something your team must fix, for your logs and never shown to the customer: the agent's configuration could not load, a call was started with no GraineEngine for the agent, a call was started while a native call holds the line, the engine page could not load after every retry, or a transport is not configured.

GraineException

What a request to Graine fails with: a typed code, a sentence written for whoever has to fix it, and, with a rate limit, how long to wait. Implements Exception; thrown by the memory and scheduling methods of GraineInApp.

Field / caseTypeDefaultMeaning
const GraineException(this.message, {this.code = GraineErrorCode.unknown, this.codeName, this.statusCode, this.retryAfterSeconds})——The constructor; the SDK builds these.
final String messageStringrequiredThe sentence Graine (or the SDK) gave, written for whoever has to fix it.
final GraineErrorCode codeGraineErrorCodeGraineErrorCode.unknownWhy — branch on this. network when Graine could not be reached; unknown for a code this build does not know (see codeName).
final String? codeNameString?nullThe code as Graine said it, including a newer one this build does not know. Null when it said none.
final int? statusCodeint?nullThe HTTP status of a refusal, when there was one.
final int? retryAfterSecondsint?nullWith rateLimited: how long Graine asked the app to wait, from the Retry-After header.
@override String toString()String—The message.

GraineErrorCode

Why Graine said no: the codes Graine sends, typed, plus network and unknown. When a refusal carries no code, the HTTP status decides: 400 invalidRequest, 401 invalidKey, 403 originRefused, 404 notFound, 429 rateLimited, 503 unavailable, anything else unknown.

Field / caseTypeDefaultMeaning
invalidKey('invalid_key')GraineErrorCode—The publishable key was rejected. Check it against Embed & Widgets in the dashboard.
originRefused('origin_refused')GraineErrorCode—The agent does not accept connections from a mobile app: add app:// to its Allowed domains.
rateLimited('rate_limited')GraineErrorCode—Too many requests. Wait retryAfterSeconds when given.
invalidRequest('invalid_request')GraineErrorCode—A field is missing or malformed. Also raised on the device for a booking reason over 120 characters and for an empty id to cancel.
identityRequired('identity_required')GraineErrorCode—Nobody is identified. Raised on the device by memories and forgetMemory, and by Graine.
deviceLimit('device_limit')GraineErrorCode—This install is not one of the user's devices.
schedulingOff('scheduling_off')GraineErrorCode—The agent does not take bookings from the app. Checked on the device.
tooSoon('too_soon')GraineErrorCode—Earlier than schedulingRules.earliest(now). Checked on the device.
tooFar('too_far')GraineErrorCode—Later than schedulingRules.latest(now). Checked on the device.
outsideWindow('outside_window')GraineErrorCode—Outside the agent's calling window.
tooManyPending('too_many_pending')GraineErrorCode—The user already has the most calls waiting that the agent allows.
notFound('not_found')GraineErrorCode—No such booking for this user or install.
unavailable('unavailable')GraineErrorCode—Graine could not answer just now. Try again with backoff.
network('network')GraineErrorCode—Graine could not be reached: offline, timed out, or the agent's configuration could not be loaded.
unknown('unknown')GraineErrorCode—A code this build does not know (its word is in GraineException.codeName), or an unexpected answer.
final String wireString—The word on the wire, as listed above.
static GraineErrorCode fromWire(String? s)GraineErrorCode—The value for a wire word (trimmed, any case); unknown for anything else.

Lower-level exported types

The package also exports the building blocks the SDK draws and connects with — the design tokens, the engine page's protocol, chat framing, loaders, placement and friction detection. They are public so a custom UI can reuse them; an app integrating the SDK does not need them. Each is listed with its members.

13.7Kotlin Multiplatform — ai.graine:inapp-kmp 0.7.0

One API in shared Kotlin over the Android and iOS SDKs. Suspending functions throw GraineException; states are StateFlows that always hold the latest value; events are SharedFlows that are not replayed.

Graine

object Graine — The SDK, and the default agent. Graine.configure(config) once at launch (Application.onCreate on Android, the app's init on iOS); every member may be called from any thread, and the suspending ones never block the main thread. Who the user is, the install, the memory choice and the screen are the app's and shared by every agent.

wireStringrequired

TooSoonSooner than the agent's minimum lead time. — wire too_soon
TooFarFurther ahead than the agent allows. — wire too_far
OutsideWindowOutside the agent's calling hours, in the user's time zone. — wire outside_window
TooManyPendingThe user already has as many calls booked as the agent allows. — wire too_many_pending
NotFound — wire not_found
UnavailableThe service could not answer just now. — wire unavailable
NetworkNo answer: no network, or Graine could not be reached. — wire network

13.8Website — the loader 1.2.0

The loader, https://www.graine.ai/embed/v1.js, defines one global, window.GraineAgent. Plain JavaScript (no build step). Every member below exists before load() is called; what needs the widget is held until it exists. Promises reject with an Error carrying code and message (and status, retryAfterSeconds when Graine answered).

GraineAgent

window.GraineAgent — loader version 1.2.0.

MemberReturnsErrorsWhat it does
load(options)Promise<boolean>Never rejects; resolves false (the console says why)Puts the agent on the page. options.agentId and options.publishableKey are required; options.variables (up to 12 keys, about 1 KB) are prompt variables. Fallbacks used only where the dashboard sets nothing: position ("bottom-right"), accent ("#318CE7"), launcherLabel ("Chat with us"), mode ("both", "voice" or "chat"). chatSize ("compact", "large" or "full") sets this page's chat window size over the dashboard's Window size. Called again with another agent, it takes the one on the page off first and resolves true once the new one is on it; with the same agent it does nothing.
version"1.2.0"—The loader's version.
switchesAgentstrue—This loader switches agents with load(). An older loader has no flag: reload the page to change agent there.
open(options)nothing—Opens the panel. Nothing happens before load() has put an agent on the page. options.mode ("chat" or "call") picks the tab among those the agent offers; options.size ("compact", "large" or "full") is for this open only. On a computer, large and full open a bigger panel (420 wide, up to 760 tall) above the launcher; on a page narrower than 640 px, large is a sheet over most of the page and full the whole page.
close()nothing—Closes the panel.
destroy()nothing—Takes the agent off the page (its frame, launcher and conversation). load() puts one back; the visitor stays identified.
defineAction(name, handler)nothing—Implements an action declared on the agent. handler(args) returns { status: "ok" | "refused" | "error", message } (or a promise of it). Answer within 5.5 seconds: after that the agent is told the page did not finish; a throw answers error; a declared action this page does not implement is refused. Safe before load().
removeAction(name)nothing—Stops offering an action — for example when a section unmounts.
setScreen(context)nothing—What the visitor can see: { screen, title, journey, fields, error, data, availableActions }. Coalesced, masked, and buffered until the widget exists.
addMaskRule(pattern, token)nothing—Adds a masking rule (a RegExp, replaced by token, default "[REDACTED]") applied before anything leaves the page, after the built-in ones.
reportEvent(event)nothing—Something worth the agent speaking up about: { name, detail }.
identify(traits, options)nothing—Who the visitor is; null signs them out of every agent they used on the page. The trait the agent's Who is the user? setting names is the identifier (never a prompt variable); other traits are masked and become prompt variables. options.memory: false: not remembered. Applies to the next conversation. Safe before load().
setMemory(enabled)nothing—Remember this visitor's conversations, or not; kept for them in this browser.
getInstallId()string—This browser's install ID, kept in localStorage (or for the page's life where storage is refused).
installId (getter)string—The same, as a property.
schedulingRules (getter)object—{ usersCanBook, minLeadMinutes, maxDaysAhead, maxPendingPerUser, ringTimeoutSeconds, callName, hostedRinging, platforms, earliest(now), latest(now) }; booking is off until load() has the agent's settings.
memories()Promise<Array<{ id, text, createdAt, updatedAt }>>identity_required, device_limit, rate_limited, network, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refusedWhat the agent remembers about the visitor, newest first (dates as Date or null).
forgetMemory()Promise<number>identity_required, device_limit, rate_limited, network, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refusedDeletes what the agent remembers about the visitor, and the kept conversation; resolves how many were deleted. Only when it succeeds, the widget's chat clears.
newConversation()Promisedevice_limit, rate_limited, network, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refusedStarts a new conversation: Graine lets go of the conversation it kept for this visitor and agent, and the widget's chat clears and opens fresh (the welcome again). Memories are untouched. Nobody identified: nothing was kept, so only the chat starts over. On a refusal the chat stays as it was.
scheduleCall(at, reason)
scheduleCall({ at, reason })		Promise<GraineScheduledCall>On the page: invalid_request (no usable at), scheduling_off, too_soon (30 seconds' grace), too_far; from Graine: outside_window, too_many_pending, identity_required, device_limit, rate_limited, network, unavailableBooks a call that rings the identified customer's app (a browser cannot ring). at: a Date, an ISO-8601 string or a timestamp; reason is trimmed to 120 characters.
scheduledCalls()Promise<GraineScheduledCall[]>network, rate_limited, unavailable, invalid_key, origin_refusedThe visitor's upcoming calls.
cancelScheduledCall(id)Promise<string>invalid_request (no id), not_found, network, rate_limited, unavailableCancels one of the visitor's calls; resolves the status afterwards, "cancelled".

GraineScheduledCall (website)

A plain object: { id, at /* Date | null */, status, source, reason, isUpcoming, canCancel } — the same fields as on every SDK; status and source are the words in GraineCallStatus and GraineCallSource.

14.Errors, limits and webhooks

14.1Error codes and their fixes

A method that asks Graine on the customer's behalf fails with one error type carrying a code. Branch on the code; show the message, which is written for the customer. Errors never carry the identifier, traits or a push token.

CodeHTTPMeansRaised byFix
invalid_key401The publishable key is not one, or belongs to no agentEvery request to GraineCopy the key again from Agent → Embed & Widgets → Install
origin_refused403The app or site is not allowed: app:// (apps) or the site's host is missing from Allowed domainsEvery requestAdd app://, or the exact host
rate_limited429Too many requests from this install, key or addressEvery requestWait retryAfterSeconds (the Retry-After header), then retry
invalid_request400A field is missing or malformed — a time without its offset, a reason over 120 charactersscheduleCall, device registrationFix the request (Flutter refuses a long reason on the device)
identity_required400No customer is identified, or the identifier is a placeholdermemories, forgetMemory, bookings that need a customeridentify() with the identifier first
device_limit403This install is not one of the customer's allowed devicesmemories, forgetMemory, newConversation, scheduleCallSign out on another device, raise Devices per user, or Reset devices for the customer
scheduling_off403 (0 on the device)Users, from your app is offscheduleCallTurn it on, or hide booking when usersCanBook is false
too_soon400 (0 on the device)Earlier than earliest(now)scheduleCallOffer times from earliest(now)
too_far400 (0 on the device)Later than latest(now)scheduleCallOffer times up to latest(now)
outside_window400Outside the agent's Calling Window (or, for agent and team bookings, inside quiet hours), in the customer's time zonescheduleCall, agent and dashboard bookingsShow the message (it names a time that works); offer another time
too_many_pending409The customer already has the most calls waitingscheduleCallCancel one first
not_found404No such booking for this customer or installcancelScheduledCallRefresh scheduledCalls()
unavailable503 (504 on a timeout)Graine could not answer just now — including a booking refused because the agent is switched off or out of creditEvery requestRetry with backoff; check the agent is on and the workspace has credit
network—No answer came back: offline, or the connection droppedEvery requestRetry when online
unknownotherA code newer than the SDK, or an unexpected answer (carrying its word)Every requestLog the code and message; show the message

When the bar or chat cannot start, the reason arrives through onError (and React Native's launcher error), not as a coded exception: key_missing, key_malformed (publishable keys start with pk_live_), key_unknown (401 — copy the key again); no_origin (403 — add app://); no_domains_configured (403 — the list is empty); origin_not_allowed (403 — add the exact host); not_configured (high-quality audio is not enabled for the workspace; calls use the standard path). A refused microphone arrives as onMicDenied("NotAllowedError") (or NotFoundError for no usable microphone); React Native and Flutter calls configured wrongly reject with invalid_options, naming the option.

14.2Rate limits and quotas

LimitValueWhere it applies
Bookings from one install10 an hourscheduleCall, and the agent's bookings in that install's conversations
Bookings in a workspace1,000 an hourAll in-app bookings
Calls waiting per customer3 by default (1–10)At most this many upcoming calls per user
Devices per customer2 by default (1–5)Devices per user; idle devices free their place after 30 days
Rings per customer per day3 by default (1–10)Ring each user at most, in the customer's own day
Quiet period after a decline6 hoursNo ring for that customer
Notice and horizon5 minutes (2–1440) · 14 days (1–30)With at least this much notice · Booked at most this far ahead
Ring time · re-ring45 s (20–60) · once after 10 min (0–120)Ring for · After a missed call, ring once more after
Lateness10 minutesA booked call more than 10 minutes late is not rung; credit and agent holds last at most 10 minutes
Booking reason · variables120 characters · 12 variables, about 1 KBBookings and calls
Memories listedAt most 100, newest firstmemories()
Conversation kept50 messages, 7 days after the lastConversations continue (0.7.0)
Requests per key and address, per minuteStarting a conversation 30 (and 300 per key); high-quality audio sessions 10 (120 per key); booking, listing, cancelling, device registration, memory list and sign-out 30 (300 per key); call outcomes 60 (600 per key); forgetting memory 10 (120 per key); listing memories also 30 per installAnswered rate_limited with Retry-After
Action handlers · component dataAbout 5 seconds · 8 secondsAfter that, the agent is told the action did not finish; a component shows its authored content

14.3Webhooks for in-app conversations

  • Where: Agent → Integrations & Tools → Custom Webhook: Webhook URL, Send these events, and the Signing secret. A subscription receives only all_processing_completed (the complete record) unless you tick more.
  • In-app and website conversations — chats, the bar's voice, native calls — are recorded in Call History like other calls, with their transcript, the screens and taps the app reported, the actions the agent took and, for a call Graine rang, the booking it came from.
  • Calls Graine rang that never became a conversation add three opt-in events — under In-app calls in Send these events: In-app call declined, In-app call missed, In-app call expired — call_declined (the customer declined a call the agent rang in your app), call_missed (it rang out unanswered) and call_expired (a scheduled in-app call could not ring in time — calling hours, credit, or the agent was off — so it was not rung). Each carries the standard envelope (event_type, event_id, timestamp, call_id, agent_id, status, sub_status, …); its status says how the ring ended. A webhook never carries the customer's identifier.

15.Data, privacy and security

15.1What leaves the phone or the page

DataWhenHow it is protected
Screen context, field values, traits, prompt variables, tracked eventsAs your app reports themMasked on the device before they leave it: PAN, Aadhaar, card and account numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, and your own patterns
The identifier (the trait Who is the user? names)Only with requests that must know the customer: starting a conversation or call, registering the device, booking, listing or cancelling calls, memory requests, signing outSent as it is (it must match), never a prompt variable, never in what the agent reads, never in a ring or a webhook
Install ID, time zone, memory choice, app and SDK versionWith the same requestsThe install ID is kept by Graine only as a one-way key
The customer's voiceOnly while a conversation or call is connected—
Typed chat messagesAs they are sentNot masked on the device: they are what the customer chose to say, kept in the conversation's transcript
Your actions' answersWhen the agent asksYour handler decides what it returns
Push tokenDevice registration, for hosted ringingStored encrypted

15.2What a ring carries

The call's ID, the agent's call name, a flag that Graine rang it, and the booking agent's ID — no reason, no variables, nothing about the customer. The reason and variables reach the agent when the call connects.

15.3What Graine stores, and for how long

WhatKeptDeleted
Push credentials (iOS Team ID, Key ID, .p8, environment; Android service account)Encrypted with your workspace's own key; never shown again or logged. The bundle ID and package name stay visibleWhen an admin presses Remove
Devices (push token, platform, app, the install's one-way key, the customer's one-way key when the device is theirs, time zone, versions, last seen)The token encrypted; the customer appears only as their one-way keyWhen Apple or Google reports the token dead; 90 days after the device was last seen. Unlinked from the customer on sign-out
Device bindingsWhich installs act as a customerSign-out, Reset devices, or 30 days unseen
The identifier on conversation recordsNormalised (trimmed, lower-cased email, last ten digits of a phone, ≤256 characters), so your team sees who each conversation was withWith the conversation record
MemoryShort facts under the one-way key, redacted before they are stored, for Keep memories for (default 1 year)On forgetMemory(), Forget this person, a single Delete this memory, or when they expire. Deleting an agent does not delete its memories early
Kept conversation (0.7.0)The last 50 messages per agent and customer7 days after the last message; on forgetting; on newConversation()
BookingsTarget (one-way keys; for a dashboard booking, the identifier typed), time, time zone, reason, status—

15.4The publishable key, and what protects it

  • The key is public by design: it ships in your page source and your app. It selects the agent; it cannot read your data or place a phone call.
  • A website request is accepted only from a host in Allowed domains; an app request only when app:// is listed.
  • Each conversation starts with a single-use connection ticket valid for two minutes.
  • Every public route is rate-limited per key, per address and, for bookings and memory, per install.
  • Memory and rings are bounded by the device limit and the customer's own sign-out. For accounts where recognising a returning customer is not enough, confirm the customer through one of your actions before the agent discusses the account.

15.5Erasure

From your app: forgetMemory() (memory and the kept conversation) and identify(null) (releases the device and unlinks it from the customer's calls). From the dashboard: Forget this person, Delete this memory, Reset devices, and Remove for push credentials.

16.Testing end to end

16.1Before you start

  • Two test customers whose identifiers you know (for example u_test_1, u_test_2), and Devices per user at its default (2).
  • At least one iPhone and two Android phones from different manufacturers — calls do not ring in simulators — plus your website on a host in Allowed domains.
  • Push credentials Verified for the exact bundle ID and package name you build (iOS development builds: environment Automatic or Sandbox).
  • Calls & scheduling: both booking switches on; a Calling Window that includes now; quiet hours that do not.
  • debug on in test builds: the SDKs log their main steps (iOS console, Android logcat tag Graine); audio, message text and variable values are never logged.
  • The dashboard's Playground runs quick checks first: the key is accepted, a made-up key is refused, the agent can call its components, a connection ticket is issued and cannot be reused, and an in-app simulator sends a screen and shows the agent's actions.

16.2The QA script

#Do thisExpect
1Phone A: sign in as customer 1; open the barThe launcher and bar in your design; the agent greets by name (from the name trait)
2Ask "what screen am I on?"; ask it to do something you declaredIt names the screen and fields; the action happens in the app and the agent says what happened
3Ask for something a component shows; tap an optionThe component appears in your design; the tap continues the conversation
4Switch to the chat and backOne conversation at a time: the call ends when the chat opens
5Tell the agent something to remember; end; start againIt remembers (allow a short while for a new fact to be stored)
6Chat a few messages; close the app; reopen the chat — then sign in as customer 1 on phone B and open the chatThe earlier messages are there on both phones (voice calls as one row each); no welcome repeated; the agent continues
7Turn memory off for customer 1 (setMemory(false)); start againNothing new remembered; nothing restored
8Sign out (identify(null)); start again; sign in as customer 2 on phone AAnonymous after sign-out: no name, no memory; then customer 2's own conversation, nothing of customer 1's
9Sign in as customer 1 on a third deviceIt works, but with no memory and device_limit from memories(); Reset devices in Memory → People frees the places
10Tap your call buttonThe call screen (CallKit on iPhone, the SDK's screen on Android); the agent knows you called (who_called = customer, call_reason)
11Ask the agent to call you back in 10 minutesIt confirms the time; Calls & scheduling → Scheduled calls lists it, Booked by the agent
12Book from the app with your booking sheet, from the website with scheduleCall, and from the dashboard with Schedule a callAll three listed (Booked by the app, Booked by Dashboard); all ring the app, not the browser
13Lock phone A and close the app; wait for a booked callIt rings on the lock screen with your call name (iPhone: the system call screen; Android: full screen, or heads-up without the full-screen permission). Answer: the agent knows why it called
14Mid-call: lock the phone, open another app, connect a Bluetooth headsetThe call goes on and follows the headset
15Decline one booked call; let another ring outdeclined then nothing for 6 hours; missed then one re-ring after your delay; webhooks call_declined / call_missed if subscribed; Android leaves a missed-call notification with Call back
16Ring during a live call (dashboard Ring now)Reported missed; the live call is untouched
17Turn on airplane mode mid-callThe call ends (ended, reason failed); it does not reconnect
18Deny the microphone; on Android 13+ deny notificationsThe bar says it needs the microphone; a booked call does not ring with the app closed
19Book for an identifier that has never used the appThe booking ends No device to ring (no_device)
20Open the second agent's screen (for example Help); chat; book a call from itIts own design, title and starters; its own conversation; the ring shows its call name and design; nothing from the first agent's chat
21Open each conversation in Call History (Monitor → Call history → Web)Each row shows User ID · u_test_1 (your field's label and value), the transcript, the screens and taps, the actions, and for rung calls the booking's outcome

16.3What each step should look like

The demo apps, run offline, show the screens the steps above produce — here the demo's care-coach use case, one of its three packs (a care coach, a banking help desk, a shop):

16.4The demo apps

Graine provides demo apps for React Native, Flutter, iOS, Android, Kotlin Multiplatform and the website, each driven by the same use-case packs (each pack is two agents: a main agent and a help agent for the Help screen). To run one against your own agent:

  1. Create the agent from the pack's setup notes. Two settings must match the pack: Memory → Who is the user? → Custom field (the pack's field, for example customer_id) and Calls & scheduling → Users, from your app (on).
  2. Allowed domains: app:// for the apps; your local host for the website (add localhost explicitly while you test, and remove it later).
  3. Put the publishable key (and optionally the help agent's) in the app's configuration file, which is not committed:
DemoConfigurationRun
React Native (Expo development build)react-native/.env: EXPO_PUBLIC_GRAINE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, EXPO_PUBLIC_GRAINE_HELP_KEY; your bundle ID and package (GRAINE_DEMO_IOS_BUNDLE_ID, GRAINE_DEMO_ANDROID_PACKAGE) and google-services.json for ringsnpm install, then npx expo run:ios --device or npx expo run:android --device
Flutterflutter/dart_defines.json: GRAINE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, GRAINE_HELP_KEY; your applicationId and bundle ID for ringsflutter pub get, then flutter run --dart-define-from-file=dart_defines.json
iOSios/Config.xcconfig: GRAINE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, GRAINE_HELP_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, DEVELOPMENT_TEAM, PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIEROpen GraineDemo.xcodeproj, run the GraineDemo scheme on a device
Androidandroid/local.properties: graine.publishableKey, graine.applicationId, graine.helpPublishableKey./gradlew :app:installDebug
Kotlin MultiplatformSee the demo's own READMEAndroid Studio (Android) and Xcode (iOS)
Websiteweb/config.jsFrom the demo folder: npx serve ., then http://localhost:3000/web/

For rings, upload push credentials for the bundle ID and package you build, then sign in as one of the pack's customers, book a call a few minutes ahead, lock the phone, and answer.

Offline mode (for screenshots, or a demo without a network): a small stand-in server, node scripts/offline-server.mjs (Node 18+, http://127.0.0.1:8790; PACK=… for another pack), answers what the SDK asks — the agent's design and settings, booked calls, memories — and plays the chat and the voice bar from the pack's script. The iOS demo connects to it with a launch argument (-GraineOffline http://127.0.0.1:8790); the website points at a stand-in loader. Nothing in offline mode is real: no model, no audio, no ringing, and a simulator has no CallKit. The screenshots above were taken this way.

17.Go-live, troubleshooting and support

17.1Go-live checklist

Dashboard

  • An agent per surface; each key in the right build; app:// and every website host (staging included) in Allowed domains; localhost removed
  • The design saved in the Garage (Assistant bar, Chat window, Call screen) and the Setup card saved
  • Actions declared and synced; components ticked under On screen; Friction tuned
  • Memory: on where wanted; Who is the user? the same field on the app's and the website's agents; Devices per user; retention and instructions
  • Calls & scheduling: call name, ring time, re-ring, rings a day, quiet hours, who may book, limits; the agent's Calling Window
  • Workspace settings → In-app calling: iOS and Android Verified for the production bundle ID and package (iOS environment Automatic or Production)
  • The prompt handles who_called (customer; scheduled for a call Graine rang; agent for your own server's ring) and call_reason, and says when to offer a call back
  • Webhooks: the events you need ticked, including call_declined, call_missed, call_expired if you track rings

Apps

  • The SDK initialised at launch; identify() after sign-in and on account switch; identify(null) on sign-out
  • Microphone declared on every platform (NSMicrophoneUsageDescription; RECORD_AUDIO, MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS where the package does not merge them)
  • iOS: Push Notifications; Background Modes Audio and Voice over IP; enableVoIPPushes() at every launch, not behind sign-in
  • Android: Firebase in the app; GraineCalls.onNewToken (or registerPushToken in React Native and Flutter) and handlePush first in your message handler; notifications asked for on Android 13+; the full-screen setting offered on Android 14+
  • A privacy screen with memories(), setMemory() and forgetMemory()
  • Store submissions: App Store review notes and privacy details; Google Play foreground-service (microphone) and full-screen-intent declarations and Data safety (section 6.8)
  • debug off in release builds

Website

  • The snippet on every page the agent belongs on; identify() on sign-in; CSP allows https://www.graine.ai

Tested

  • The QA script (section 16.2) on an iPhone, two Android phones and the website, signed in as known test customers

17.2Troubleshooting

What you seeWhy, and what to do
Nothing appears in the app; the log says 403 / no_originapp:// is missing from the agent's Allowed domains
Nothing appears on the websiteThe exact host (with or without www.) is not in Allowed domains, or the key was rotated — copy the new snippet
The launcher appears but the agent never answersThe agent has no web-call variant yet: save the agent once
The bar says it needs the microphone, and no dialog appearedThe permission is not declared (RECORD_AUDIO, or NSMicrophoneUsageDescription on iOS), or the customer refused it before; Flutter: requestMicrophone is not set
iOS: the app closes as a call startsNSMicrophoneUsageDescription is missing
Android: a call stays on "Connecting…"Your activity does not forward onRequestPermissionsResult to the SDK
The agent does not know the screensetScreen is not called on that screen or on every change; React Native: navigationRef is not the same ref as the NavigationContainer
"Sorry, I can't do that here"The action is not declared on the agent, or the names differ
No componentNot ticked under On screen, not named in the prompt (or the step), or not synced to the agent
The agent does not remember someoneThe app passes a different trait from the one Who is the user? names; the value is a placeholder; memory is off for them; or this is one device too many
The same person shows up twiceThe identifier differs between devices (an ID on one, an email on the other) or its case changed
device_limit for a real customerThey use more devices than you allow: raise Devices per user, or Reset devices
A booked call never ringsCredentials not Verified for this bundle ID or package; a simulator; iOS: enableVoIPPushes() not called at launch; Android: onNewToken not forwarded, no google-services.json, or notifications not allowed; or the customer has not opened the app signed in for 30 days (no_device)
iOS: rings on development builds but not TestFlightThe environment is Sandbox: choose Automatic or Production
iOS: VoIP pushes stopped arriving altogetherAn app that fails to report a VoIP push to CallKit loses them; call enableVoIPPushes() at every launch and send VoIP pushes only for calls
Android: a heads-up notification instead of a full-screen ringAndroid 14+ without the full-screen permission. It still rings; offer the setting
Android: rings only while the app is openhandlePush is not the first thing in onMessageReceived, or notifications are not allowed
A call stops soon after the screen locksA phone's battery saver: ask the customer to allow your app in battery settings
A call rang later than bookedIt fell outside the Calling Window or inside quiet hours in the customer's time zone and moved to the next opening
The design did not changeApps read the design at start: restart the app. Websites read it at page load
Every booking refused with unavailableThe agent is switched off, or the workspace is out of credit

17.3Support

Write to support@graine.ai or use https://www.graine.ai/support. Include the platform and SDK version, the agent's ID (never the key's secret parts — the publishable key is public), the time of the event with its time zone, the call's ID (call_… or the booking's ID) and the SDK's debug log. Do not send customer identifiers or push tokens by email. The online documentation is at https://www.graine.ai/docs/in-app.
